fix_subject: net/iavf: fix crash in Tx drain on PF reset
fix_message:
net/iavf: fix crash in Tx drain on PF reset

The Tx cleanup helpers check the DD bit of the descriptor at the next RS
boundary and assume software has already posted it. The burst path
guarantees this by only cleaning up when nb_tx_free drops below
tx_free_thresh, but iavf_dev_tx_drain() called the helpers on any
non-empty queue.

With fewer than tx_rs_thresh descriptors outstanding, that descriptor
still held the DESC_DONE value set by reset_tx_queue(), so the helpers
treated the block as complete and freed NULL (or already freed) mbufs,
crashing on PF reset.

Only clean up a queue once a full RS block is outstanding.

fix_subject: net/hns3: fix hard-coded default value of UMV space
fix_message:
net/hns3: fix hard-coded default value of UMV space

Currently, the driver obtains the PF's UMV (unicast MAC VLAN) table
space from the board configuration, and falls back to the hard-coded
default value HNS3_DEFAULT_UMV_SPACE_PER_PF (384 = 3072 / 8) when
the firmware reports an empty umv_space field.

The hard-coded value is only accurate for chips with a 3072-entry UMV
table. On chips whose total UMV table size is smaller than 3072, every
PF still requests 384 entries: the first initialized PF occupies the
whole table while the others get nothing, which makes adding unicast
MAC or VLAN entries fail on those ports.

Fix this by obtaining the UMV size from the device specifications
command, whose umv_size field is the default value allocated by the
firmware policy. The requested size is determined at allocation time
in hns3_init_umv_space(), in the following priority:
  1. pf->cfg_umv_size, the user specified value from the board
     configuration
  2. pf->def_umv_size, the default value reported by the firmware
  3. the hard-coded default, as the last fallback for old firmware

Fixes: d51867db65c1 ("net/hns3: add initialization")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

fix_subject: net/tap: fix FD leak on netns change
fix_message:
net/tap: fix FD leak on netns change

When a tap interface moves to another namespace, tap_netns_change()
calls tap_lsc_intr_handle_set(dev, 1) to recreate the LSC interrupt
without first tearing down the old one. The previous LSC netlink
socket fd is never closed.

Defer the full LSC teardown and re-registration to an alarm callback
which runs in the interrupt thread but outside any active source
context. The alarm switches to the device's network namespace, tears
down the old LSC handle, sets up a new one (opening a fresh netlink
socket in the correct namespace), restores the original namespace,
and forces carrier state back up.

Extract tap_dev_ns_switch/tap_dev_ns_restore helpers to share the
namespace switch logic between tap_netns_change and the alarm.

Fixes: aae3a38e9e03 ("net/tap: detect namespace change")

fix_subject: drivers: fix ASan ODR violation on mlx glue symbols
fix_message:
drivers: fix ASan ODR violation on mlx glue symbols

With ibverbs linked by dlopen, a static PMD and its glue library
each define one global. net/mlx4 and librte_net_mlx4_glue both
define mlx4_glue. common/mlx5 and librte_common_mlx5_glue both
define mlx5_glue. This is not a clash between mlx4 and mlx5.

Only AddressSanitizer detects this collision. The linker keeps one
copy, so a normal process is unaffected. AddressSanitizer records
both definitions and aborts at startup.

Keep the name dlsym() looks up in the glue library. Point the PMD
at that table through a private symbol.

fix_subject: net/mlx5: fix write-after-read in flow modify action
fix_message:
net/mlx5: fix write-after-read in flow modify action

In HWS non-root groups, modify field actions are compiled into a
modify header pattern. When a COPY or ADD_FIELD reads a field and the
next SET or ADD writes that same field, no NOP was inserted between
them. Firmware rejects the resulting pattern at template table
creation with syndrome 0xa0a3a8.

flow_hw_should_insert_nop() only compared the new command's
destination with the previous command's destination. After a
COPY or ADD_FIELD it never compared against the previous source
field, which is the one that was read.

Extend the checks so a NOP is inserted when:
- a SET or ADD writes a field read by the previous COPY or ADD_FIELD,
- a COPY or ADD_FIELD writes a field read by the previous COPY or
  ADD_FIELD.

Two consecutive reads of the same field still do not need a NOP.

Fixes: 0f4aa72b99da ("net/mlx5: support flow modify field with HWS")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

fix_subject: net/iavf: fix memory leaks in RSS flow engine
fix_message:
net/iavf: fix memory leaks in RSS flow engine

This patch addresses several memory leaks and incorrect error reporting
that exist in the iavf RSS (hash) flow engine:

- iavf_hash_parse_raw_pattern() returns without freeing "pkt_buf" when
  the "msk_buf" allocation fails, leaking the first buffer on every
  failed raw pattern parse.

- iavf_hash_create() only frees the parsed "meta" on success.  Both
  error paths return early and leak the struct iavf_rss_meta allocated
  by iavf_hash_parse_pattern_action(), which no other caller frees.
  Free in both error paths.

- iavf_hash_destroy() never releases flow->rule.  The virtchnl_rss_cfg
  allocated by iavf_hash_create() is only released by the engine's free
  callback, iavf_hash_free(), which is invoked from iavf_flow_uninit()
  but not from iavf_flow_destroy().  So every flow destroy or flush of
  an RSS rule leaks it.  The early return taken while the VF is
  resetting leaks it too.  Free the config and clear flow->rule properly
  in all paths.

- Out of memory conditions are reported to the application as EINVAL
  while -ENOMEM is returned.  Report ENOMEM instead.

Fixes: bc0e85586eaf ("net/iavf: support VF RSS flow rule with raw pattern")
Fixes: 7be10c3004be ("net/iavf: add RSS configuration for VF")
Fixes: c02ea7410e51 ("net/iavf: fix flow flush after PF reset")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Anurag Mandal <anurag.mandal@intel.com>
Acked-by: Bruce Richardson <bruce.richardson@intel.com>

fix_subject: net/gve: fix DQO Tx report event interval
fix_message:
net/gve: fix DQO Tx report event interval

A descriptor completion is requested once every 32 packets, and Tx
descriptors are only reclaimed on these completions. With
multi-segment or TSO packets the ring can fill before 32 packets are
posted, so no completion is ever requested and the Tx queue stalls
for good.

Request a completion once GVE_TX_MIN_RE_INTERVAL descriptors have
been posted since the last one, as the Linux driver does.

Fixes: 4022f9999f56 ("net/gve: support basic Tx data path for DQO")
Fixes: 403c671a46b6 ("net/gve: support TSO in DQO RDA")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

fix_subject: net/gve: fix TSO segment offset calculation
fix_message:
net/gve: fix TSO segment offset calculation

The descriptor limit validation for TSO packets was erroneously
computing the TSO segment offset at the end of an mbuf. The first bytes
of any mbuf will be included as part of the previous TSO segment which
has not yet been completed, as indicated by seg_remain. Subtract those
seg_remain bytes from the mbuf length before computing the segment
offset.

Visual representation:

Before:
------------------------------------------------------------------
|    tso_    |    tso_    |    tso_    |    tso_    |    tso_    |
|    segsz   |    segsz   |    segsz   |    segsz   |    segsz   |
------------------------------------------------------------------
|           16K               |            16K               |   |
------------------------------------------------------------------

After:
------------------------------------------------------------------
|rem |    tso_    |    tso_    |    tso_    |    tso_    | seg_  |
|ain |    segsz   |    segsz   |    segsz   |    segsz   |offset |
------------------------------------------------------------------
|           16K               |            16K               |   |
------------------------------------------------------------------
                                                               ^
                                                        mbuf_remain

In this example, the original code would have found that tso_segsz
evenly divides mbuf_len, and that there is no tail to be considered
split across two mbufs. So the number of descriptors it would have found
would be:

  1 (for the headers) +
  0 (no segment offset) +
  0 (mbuf_remain cannot be less than 0)

For a total of one descriptor counted in num_descs for the start of
the current TSO segment.

Meanwhile, the reality would be:

  1 (for the headers) +
  1 (seg_offset != 0) +
  1 (mbuf_remain < seg_offset)

For a total of 3 descriptors counted against the descriptor limit.

This undercount can cause TSO segments to incorrectly cross up to two
extra descriptors more than the hardware limit, leading to the datapath
being disabled.

Fixes: be8f0eb81f98 ("net/gve: fix DQO TSO descriptor limit")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Joshua Washington <joshwash@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Ankit Garg <nktgrg@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Praveen Kaligineedi <pkaligineedi@google.com>

fix_subject: net/gve: fix Tx stall on invalid packets
fix_message:
net/gve: fix Tx stall on invalid packets

When a packet fails rte_mbuf_check() or exceeds the descriptor limit,
the Tx burst stops at that packet without consuming it. The
application retries the same packet, it fails again, and the queue
never moves.

Free such packets and continue with the burst. Validate before the
ring space check, so that an oversized packet is dropped instead of
stopping the burst there. Count rte_mbuf_check() failures in a new
invalid_mbufs counter.

Fixes: f4a70b449bfa ("net/gve: add DQO Tx descriptor limit")
Fixes: f33ce4445ee6 ("net/gve: validate Tx packet before sending")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

fix_subject: ethdev: add missing action types to flow conversion
fix_message:
ethdev: add missing action types to flow conversion

RTE_FLOW_ACTION_TYPE_SHARED, RTE_FLOW_ACTION_TYPE_METER_COLOR and
RTE_FLOW_ACTION_TYPE_SKIP_CMAN were never added to
rte_flow_desc_action[]. The table uses designated initializers, so
these slots are zero filled: their name is NULL and their size is
zero.

As a result, RTE_FLOW_CONV_OP_ACTION_NAME on any of them passes a
NULL source to strlcpy(), and rte_flow_copy() as well as the action
conversion operations reject any action list containing one of them
as an unknown action type.

Add the missing descriptor entries. Preserve the deprecated SHARED
action handle directly, as for INDIRECT, instead of treating it as
configuration data to copy into the destination buffer.

fix_message:
ethdev: add missing action types to flow conversion

RTE_FLOW_ACTION_TYPE_SHARED, RTE_FLOW_ACTION_TYPE_METER_COLOR and
RTE_FLOW_ACTION_TYPE_SKIP_CMAN were never added to
rte_flow_desc_action[]. The table uses designated initializers, so
these slots are zero filled: their name is NULL and their size is
zero.

As a result, RTE_FLOW_CONV_OP_ACTION_NAME on any of them passes a
NULL source to strlcpy(), and rte_flow_copy() as well as the action
conversion operations reject any action list containing one of them
as an unknown action type.

Add the missing descriptor entries. Preserve the deprecated SHARED
action handle directly, as for INDIRECT, instead of treating it as
configuration data to copy into the destination buffer.

Fixes: 4d9fd85fb545 ("ethdev: add shared actions to flow API")
Fixes: 5f0d54f372f0 ("ethdev: add pre-defined meter policy API")
Fixes: 6807e8b52a18 ("ethdev: skip congestion management configuration")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Anatoly Burakov <anatoly.burakov@intel.com>

fix_subject: net/iavf: fix watchdog clearing reset state during recovery
fix_message:
net/iavf: fix watchdog clearing reset state during recovery

Since the watchdog is kept armed across a PF reset, it can clear the
`vf_reset` flag while the reset event is still queued or being handled,
as VFGEN_RSTAT toggles while the PF resets the VF. iavf_dev_close() then
skips re-enabling PCI bus mastering, which the VF reset cleared, so
VIRTCHNL_OP_VERSION never reaches the PF, iavf_dev_init() fails and the
port is left returning -EIO. Each toggle also posts a further reset
event, causing redundant recovery cycles.

Count reset events from before `vf_reset` is set until they have been
handled, and do not let the watchdog clear the flag while any are
outstanding. Also make the `vf_reset` flag atomic, as it is accessed
from multiple places: the watchdog alarm, the interrupt thread and the
virtchnl polling path.

Fixes: a0e296420a70 ("net/iavf: keep watchdog armed for the whole reset window")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Suggested-by: Declan Doherty <declan.doherty@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Ciara Loftus <ciara.loftus@intel.com>
Acked-by: Bruce Richardson <bruce.richardson@intel.com>

fix_subject: net/iavf: fix null engine for egress security flows
fix_message:
net/iavf: fix null engine for egress security flows

Egress security flows bypass the flow parsers and are inserted with a
NULL `engine` pointer. The create path then dereferences that pointer

fix_subject: net/txgbe: keep flow rules per port
fix_message:
net/txgbe: keep flow rules per port

rte_flow rules for every txgbe port were stored in file-scope lists.
Flushing or closing one port freed the rte_flow handles of the others
while their hardware rules stayed programmed, and probing another port

fix_subject: vdpa/mlx5: fix RSS flow leak on steering update failure
fix_message:
vdpa/mlx5: fix RSS flow leak on steering update failure

mlx5_vdpa_steer_update() calls mlx5_vdpa_rss_flows_create() which, on
failure, leaves behind any RSS steering objects (matcher, TIR, TIR
action, flow) it managed to create before the error, relying on the
caller to release them.

mlx5_vdpa_steer_setup() honors that contract by calling
mlx5_vdpa_steer_unset() on its error path, but mlx5_vdpa_virtq_enable()
only logs a warning and continues when mlx5_vdpa_steer_update() fails.
As a result, every failed steering update triggered from the virtq
enable/disable path leaks the partially created software-steering
objects. Over many reconfiguration cycles this exhausts the kernel
software-steering (DR) resources and later probes fail with
"Failed to create Rx domain".

Free the partial RSS flows in mlx5_vdpa_steer_update() itself so that
all callers are covered regardless of how they handle the return value.
mlx5_vdpa_rss_flows_destroy() checks each object for NULL, so the
subsequent steer_unset() on the steer_setup() error path stays a safe
no-op.

Fixes: 9f09b1ca15c5 ("vdpa/mlx5: recreate a virtq becoming enabled")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Maayan Kashani <mkashani@nvidia.com>
Acked-by: Dariusz Sosnowski <dsosnowski@nvidia.com>

fix_subject: gro: fix returned packet count after UDP fragment merge
fix_message:
gro: fix returned packet count after UDP fragment merge

rte_gro_reassemble_burst() decrements nb_after_gro only for packets that
are merged while being inserted into the reassembly tables. When the
tables are flushed at the end of the burst, gro_udp4_tbl_timeout_flush()
and gro_vxlan_udp4_tbl_timeout_flush() call gro_udp4_merge_items(), which
merges fragments that became adjacent only after an intermediate fragment
arrived. Such merges are not reflected in nb_after_gro, but they are
accounted for in the local index i, which after the flush holds the
actual number of packets written to pkts[].

The function returns nb_after_gro regardless. When a flush-time merge
happens, the caller is told there are more packets than were actually
produced: the surplus pkts[] entries point to mbufs that are already
chained into an earlier packet. Freeing the returned burst then frees
those mbufs twice and corrupts the mempool, and the surplus entry, whose
headers have been stripped by the merge, is handed back to the caller as
a standalone packet built from fragment payload.

Return the actual packet count i instead. In the path where the flush
block is skipped, i equals nb_pkts, which also equals nb_after_gro, so
the non-merging case is unchanged.

Fixes: 74080d7dcf31 ("gro: support IPv6 for TCP")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Andrey Mokrushin <a.mokrushin@ideco.ru>

fix_subject: net/bnxt/tf_core: fix buffer leaks in RM create DB
fix_message:
net/bnxt/tf_core: fix buffer leaks in RM create DB

tf_rm_create_db() allocates a capabilities query buffer, a copy of
the requested counts, and the request and reservation arrays.
The query buffer is never freed: not on success, not on the common
error exit, and not on the early error returns. The early returns
also leak whichever of the other buffers had been allocated by that
point, and the rm_db structure when the element array allocation
fails.

Free the query buffer on success and on the existing error path, and
send the early error returns through a common label that frees the
temporary buffers and returns the original error code.

Fixes: ced3cded4492 ("net/bnxt: update table get to use new design")
Fixes: 7052999153f2 ("net/bnxt: add action SRAM translation")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Manish Kurup <manish.kurup@broadcom.com>

fix_subject: common/cnxk: fix use-after-free during MACsec teardown
fix_message:
common/cnxk: fix use-after-free during MACsec teardown

The idev mcs_list is walked from the mailbox interrupt thread via
roc_idev_mcs_get() and dereferenced in mcs_event_cb_process(), while
the control thread can concurrently free the mcs in roc_mcs_dev_fini().
With no lock on the list, an MCS interrupt during teardown could read
freed memory or corrupt the TAILQ mid-splice.

Add a dedicated idev mcs_lock, held across the lookup+callback in the
interrupt handler, the list insert in roc_mcs_dev_init(), and the
TAILQ_REMOVE in roc_mcs_dev_fini() (which drains any in-flight
interrupt before mcs and sa_port_map are freed). List helpers stay
lock-free to avoid recursive locking.

Fixes: f752780f30dc ("common/cnxk: add ROC MACsec initialization")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Aarnav JP <ajp@marvell.com>

fix_subject: common/mlx5: fix memory key relaxed ordering
fix_message:
common/mlx5: fix memory key relaxed ordering

The updated device specification defines relaxed ordering as 0x1 and
reserves 0x2. Update the mkey read-after-write ordering values
accordingly.

Windows MR registration applies full MKC ordering, including
read-after-write, on every non-Haswell CPU. Other mlx5 drivers apply
that ordering only when firmware reports relaxed-order-only mode.
Keep relaxed-ordering read and write enabled from HCA capabilities, and
apply read-after-write ordering only when
mkc_order_write_after_write_ro_only is set.

Fixes: 5003eaab7e49 ("common/mlx5: update relaxed ordering policy for mkeys")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

fix_subject: net/ixgbe: fix L4 protocol parsing for ntuple
fix_message:
net/ixgbe: fix L4 protocol parsing for ntuple

Currently, when parsing ntuple flows, we may hit an empty L4 protocol
item (i.e. one that does not have a mask or spec), in which case we just
skip to the end. However, we do not set a protocol mask, which means we
will not be matching L4 flows even though the flow structure implies
that we should.

Fix it by setting up match-by-protocol when we have an empty L4 flow.

Additionally, there's a separate issue with how empty L4 protocol items
are handled in that once we see one, we do not check whether there's
anything else past it, and instead go straight to exit. This means that
we might have any other flow item after L4 (e.g. ipv4 / tcp / gtp) and
this will be silently accepted. Fix by enforcing that last item is END.

Fixes: 46ea969177f3 ("net/ixgbe: add ntuple support to flow parser")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Anatoly Burakov <anatoly.burakov@intel.com>
Acked-by: Vladimir Medvedkin <vladimir.medvedkin@intel.com>

fix_subject: net/bnxt: use long descriptors for Tx checksum offload
fix_message:
net/bnxt: use long descriptors for Tx checksum offload

Commit 2feea0f3b8b0 ("net/bnxt: modify check for short Tx BD") removed
the TCP, UDP and IP checksum flags from bnxt_xmit_need_long_bd().
The checksum flags are written to the second descriptor
(txbd1->lflags), which only exists for a long BD.
With only checksum offload requested, the packet now uses a short BD
that carries no checksum flags, so the hardware does not compute the
checksums and packets with bad checksums are forwarded unchanged.

Request a long BD again when TCP, UDP or IP checksum offload is set.

Fixes: 2feea0f3b8b0 ("net/bnxt: modify check for short Tx BD")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Mohammad Shuab Siddique <mohammad-shuab.siddique@broadcom.com>

fix_subject: net/gve: enforce DQO TSO header and length limits
fix_message:
net/gve: enforce DQO TSO header and length limits

TSO packets are not checked against the device limits before use.
The device requires an MSS of 88 to 9728 bytes and a payload of at
most 262143 bytes, as noted in the Linux driver. A packet outside
these limits triggers malicious driver detection, which drops it and
disables the datapath, stalling all queues.

The missing checks also break the driver itself: a tso_segsz of 0
divides by zero in gve_tx_validate_descs(), headers longer than 255
bytes are truncated by the 8-bit header_len field, and headers not
contained in the first segment give gve_tx_validate_descs() a
negative first segment length.

Drop TSO packets that violate these limits and count them as
invalid_pkts.

Fixes: 403c671a46b6 ("net/gve: support TSO in DQO RDA")
Fixes: be8f0eb81f98 ("net/gve: fix DQO TSO descriptor limit")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Tathagat Priyadarshi <tathagat.dpdk@gmail.com>

fix_subject: net/failsafe: fix MAC address pool size and replay
fix_message:
net/failsafe: fix MAC address pool size and replay

Two issues affect fail-safe MAC address handling:

- fs_mac_addr_add() grew the pool but set nb_mac_addr to the index of
  the new entry instead of the entry count (index + 1). The pool size
  was off by one and the last added address was dropped when the
  configuration was replayed to a sub-device.

- fs_eth_dev_conf_apply() replayed every slot of the MAC address array
  to a (re)plugged sub-device, including slots left zeroed by a
  previous remove, which made rte_eth_dev_mac_addr_add() fail on the
  all-zero address.

Set nb_mac_addr to index + 1 and skip zeroed slots when replaying the
MAC addresses.

Fixes: a46f8d584eb8 ("net/failsafe: add fail-safe PMD")
Fixes: ebea83f899d8 ("net/failsafe: add plug-in support")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Sandeep Penigalapati <sandeep.penigalapati@intel.com>

fix_subject: eal/linux: fix dirty flag for reused hugepages in legacy mem
fix_message:
eal/linux: fix dirty flag for reused hugepages in legacy mem

With --huge-unlink=never the hugepage files are kept and mapped again
on the next run. The kernel only zeroes a hugepage the first time it is
mapped from a given file, so these pages still hold the previous run's
content.

The dynamic memory path records this by setting RTE_MEMSEG_FLAG_DIRTY
in alloc_seg(). The legacy path in remap_segment() never sets ms->flags,
so rte_zmalloc_socket() skips the memset and returns stale data.

With --legacy-mem --huge-unlink=never, a second process gets non-zeroed
memory from rte_zmalloc(). mlx5 with sys_mem_en disabled allocates its
internal structures through rte_zmalloc_socket() and then reads stale
pointers from them, which crashes in mlx5_ipool_malloc_cache() during
probe:

  SEGV on unknown address 0x000000000308
    #0 _mlx5_ipool_malloc_cache drivers/net/mlx5/mlx5_utils.c:550
    ...
    #16 mlx5_alloc_shared_dr drivers/net/mlx5/linux/mlx5_os.c:628

Set RTE_MEMSEG_FLAG_DIRTY on segments remapped in legacy mode whenever
existing hugepage files are reused, matching the dynamic path. Why a
reused page is dirty is documented on unlink_existing.

Fixes: 32b4771cd8ef ("eal/linux: allow hugepage file reuse")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Maayan Kashani <mkashani@nvidia.com>
Acked-by: Dmitry Kozlyuk <dmitry.kozliuk@gmail.com>

fix_subject: app/testpmd: fix VXLAN-GPE and GENEVE custom port parsing
fix_message:
app/testpmd: fix VXLAN-GPE and GENEVE custom port parsing

The csum forwarding engine parses packets with rte_net_get_ptype(),
which recognizes VXLAN-GPE and GENEVE tunnels only on their default UDP
ports. Since the switch to that API, --vxlan-gpe-port and
--geneve-parsed-port no longer take effect: a packet whose outer UDP
destination port matches a configured non-default port is not detected
as a tunnel, so tunnel Tx flags, outer checksum handling and tunnel TSO
are skipped.

When parse-tunnel is enabled, temporarily map a configured port to the
corresponding default while calling rte_net_get_ptype(), then restore the
packet. If an option replaces a default port, hide that default from the
parser to preserve the options' previous behavior. Plain VXLAN is
unchanged: the csum engine has always recognized it only on
RTE_VXLAN_DEFAULT_PORT, and rx_vxlan_port configures the device filter
rather than this parser.

Only process inner checksums when the parser identified an inner IP
header and all declared inner headers fit in the first segment. This
preserves tunnel forwarding for valid non-IP payloads and avoids
accessing truncated or non-contiguous inner headers on both default and
configured tunnel ports.

Fixes: 76730c7b9b5a ("app/testpmd: use packet type parsing API")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

fix_subject: common/mlx5: fix high SMMU TLB miss with mempool alignment
fix_message:
common/mlx5: fix high SMMU TLB miss with mempool alignment

On Kunpeng SoC with mlx CX7, dpdk-l3fwd with intra-NUMA core pinning
under SMMU nonstrict/strict mode shows about 30% performance degradation
compared to cross-NUMA pinning. With SMMU disabled or passthrough mode,
intra-NUMA performs as expected (slightly better than cross-NUMA).

CX7 in NUMA1
NUMA node0 CPU(s):    0-39
NUMA node1 CPU(s):    40-79

intra-NUMA:
dpdk-l3fwd -l 40-55 -n 4 -a 0000:17:00.1,mprq_en=1 -- -p 0x1 -P \
   --config='(0,0,40),(0,1,41),(0,2,42),(0,3,43),(0,4,44),\
             (0,5,45),(0,6,46),(0,7,47),(0,8,48),(0,9,49),\
             (0,10,50),(0,11,51),(0,12,52),(0,13,53),\
             (0,14,54),(0,15,55)' \
   --rx-queue-size=4096 --tx-queue-size=4096 --rx-burst=64

cross-NUMA:
dpdk-l3fwd -l 11-26 -n 4 -a 0000:17:00.1,mprq_en=1 -- -p 0x1 -P \
   --config='(0,0,11),(0,1,12),(0,2,13),(0,3,14),(0,4,15),\
             (0,5,16),(0,6,17),(0,7,18),(0,8,19),(0,9,20),\
             (0,10,21),(0,11,22),(0,12,23),(0,13,24),\
             (0,14,25),(0,15,26)' \
   --rx-queue-size=4096 --tx-queue-size=4096 --rx-burst=64

The root cause is that under SMMU enabled mode, the mempool allocated
for intra-NUMA pinning is aligned to system page size instead of
hugepage size, while cross-NUMA pinning correctly uses hugepage size
alignment. This causes high TLB miss rates under SMMU.

For non-external memory, align all memory ranges to hugepage boundaries
during mempool registration to ensure hugepage_sz alignment, thereby
reducing TLB misses and fixing the intra-NUMA performance degradation.
External memory keeps the original behavior.

Fixes: 690b2a88c2f7 ("common/mlx5: add mempool registration facilities")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Shuaisong Yang <yangshuaisong@h-partners.com>
Signed-off-by: Xingui Yang <yangxingui@huawei.com>
Acked-by: Viacheslav Ovsiienko <viacheslavo@nvidia.com>

fix_subject: net/ixgbe: fix ntuple filter priority
fix_message:
net/ixgbe: fix ntuple filter priority

Currently, handling of ntuple filter priority is incorrect: it directly
translates values inside the valid range (001b-111b), and clamps all
invalid to 1. This leads to equivalence between rte_flow highest
priority value (0), and rte_flow lower priority values (8+), both of
which are mapped to 1 (lowest priority), while the 1-7 range is reversed
(in ntuple, 111b is highest priority, but in rte_flow it is the lowest).

Fix the calculation by

- Translating highest rte_flow priority to highest ntuple priority
- Only clamping low priority values to 1 (lowest priority)
- Reversing the 1-7 mapping to preserve semantic meaning

fix_subject: net/mana: fix Tx burst error handling
fix_message:
net/mana: fix Tx burst error handling

mana_tx_burst() skipped, using continue, a packet that exceeded the
segment limit or whose SGL could not be populated. rte_eth_tx_burst()
callers treat the return value as a contiguous prefix of consumed
packets, so later packets were posted while the caller considered them
unsent and freed them, and their completions then freed them again.

Drop such a packet instead: count it in stats.errors, free it and
include it in the returned count. Return early only when the ring is
full, since a packet that fails validation would fail again on every
retry and stall applications that loop until all packets are sent.

sgl.gdma_sgl[] holds MAX_SGL_ENTRIES_FOR_TRANSMIT entries, but
max_send_sge comes from the device and was not limited, so a packet with
more segments could write past the array. Reject such packets and limit
the advertised nb_seg_max and nb_mtu_seg_max to the same value.

Fixes: 7f322844f427 ("net/mana: send packets")
Fixes: d878cb09501d ("net/mana: report device info")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Tathagat Priyadarshi <tathagat.dpdk@gmail.com>

expected ':', ',', ';', '}' or '__attribute__' before '__counted_by'

fix_subject: lpm: fix SVE bulk lookup loop bound for small bursts
fix_message:
lpm: fix SVE bulk lookup loop bound for small bursts

In __rte_lpm_lookup_vec() (SVE), the main loop condition was

    for (i = 0; i < n - vl; i += vl)

where n is uint32_t and vl is uint64_t. When n < vl the subtraction
is done in 64-bit unsigned arithmetic and wraps to a very large
value, so the loop does not terminate at the end of the input array.
It reads past the end of ips[] resulting in a segmentation fault.

Rewrite the condition as "i + vl < n" so no unsigned wrap occurs. The
existing tail handling with svwhilelt_b32() covers the remaining
elements, including n == 0.

Fixes: b29ccbea24ae ("lpm: use SVE for bulk lookup")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Rupesh Chiluka <rchiluka@marvell.com>

fix_subject: ip_frag: fix IPv6 fragmentation of short packets
fix_message:
ip_frag: fix IPv6 fragmentation of short packets

rte_ipv6_fragment_packet() does not check that the first mbuf segment
is large enough to hold the IPv6 header, unlike the IPv4 version,
which validates data_len against the header length.

With data_len < 40, in_seg_data_pos starts past the end of the
segment, the expression (in_seg->data_len - in_seg_data_pos)
underflows and the loop never advances to the next segment, so it
keeps producing fragments and writing past the end of pkts_out.

Reject such packets with -EINVAL, as rte_ipv4_fragment_packet() does.

Fixes: 0aa31d7a5929 ("ip_frag: add IPv6 fragmentation support")

fix_subject: net/mana: fix Rx interrupt handling on lock contention
fix_message:
net/mana: fix Rx interrupt handling on lock contention

Rx interrupt enable and disable take the per-device reset_ops_lock
with a trylock and return -EBUSY when it is held. Every Rx queue
takes that lock on each enable and disable, so with two or more
queues on different lcores the calls collide routinely. A failed
enable leaves the CQ unarmed, and a thread that then sleeps in
rte_epoll_wait() is not woken by the next packet; it sleeps until
its timeout with packets in the ring. A failed disable leaves the
event unconsumed. Applications do not expect -EBUSY from these
calls outside a reset, and l3fwd-power ignores the return value.

Seen on Azure (MANA VF) with 2 queues and a 10 ms epoll timeout:
about 550 lost wakeups per queue in one run, p99 latency 9.9 ms,
and 22.7% packet loss at the higher rate tested. With one queue
there was no loss.

The section under the lock is a doorbell write or a non-blocking
read of the completion channel, so wait for the lock instead.
The device state check is kept, so the calls still return -EBUSY
while a reset is in progress; a caller that arrives while the reset
thread holds the lock waits for that step to finish first.

Fixes: 077ca514d641 ("net/mana: support device reset")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Orgad Shaneh <orgads@gmail.com>

fix_subject: net/txgbe: fix 40G FFE tuning applied to first lane only
fix_message:
net/txgbe: fix 40G FFE tuning applied to first lane only

On the 40G NIC, an FFE value only reaches the first of the four
lanes: the E56 PHY holds one FFE byte per lane, but the tuned taps
were written as a single byte value, so the other three lanes keep
their default equalizer setting and the received signal on them can
be degraded.

Use the E56 PHY FFE defaults on the 40G NIC and replicate each tap
value over the four lanes. The FFE fields grow to 32 bits to hold
the replicated value, and the devargs are parsed after the shared
code init so the MAC type is known when the 40G defaults are picked.

Fixes: 6104fd11086e ("net/txgbe: fix link stability for 25G NIC")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Zaiyu Wang <zaiyuwang@trustnetic.com>

fix_subject: net/txgbe: fix link state in 10G forced mode
fix_message:
net/txgbe: fix link state in 10G forced mode

When an AML40 port is configured in 10G forced mode (auto_neg=0),
the hardware can link up but the driver keeps reporting link down
after a peer link failure: link_valid is cleared on timeout but
never restored when the peer recovers, so the link stays down until
the port is restarted.

Restore hw->link_valid = true in the success path of
txgbe_setup_phy_link_aml40(), symmetric to the 40G path. Handle
TXGBE_ERR_PHY_INIT_NOT_DONE before the timeout split and leave
link_valid untouched, matching the 25G path in
txgbe_setup_phy_link_aml(); the alarm retry then attempts the
setup again.

Fixes: f7cfc21e9f75 ("net/txgbe: fix link stability for 40G NIC")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

fix_subject: fib6: fix temporary tbl8 for byte-aligned prefixes
fix_message:
fib6: fix temporary tbl8 for byte-aligned prefixes

Currently, `install_to_dp()` builds one tbl8 level more than a route
range needs when the range ends on a byte boundary. If the range
spans a whole table at its first uncommon byte, e.g. a /32 or a /40,
`build_common_root()` allocates a tbl8 one level too deep, all of
its entries get the same next hop and `recycle_root_path()` frees it
again. Below /24, an edge aligned on /24, e.g. of a /16, gets a tbl8 that
`write_edge()` fills and recycles at once.

These temporary tbl8s are not covered by `rsvd_tbl8s`, which counts
only the levels the route set keeps. With a nearly full pool, an add
that passed the reservation check runs out of tbl8s in the middle of the
install, the tbl8 already linked into the dataplane is leaked and a later
add that fits is refused. A /32 can not be added to a pool of one tbl8,
nor deleted from a full pool.

Fix it by not building these levels.

Bugzilla ID: 1970
Fixes: c3e12e0f0354 ("fib: add dataplane algorithm for IPv6")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Reported-by: Maxime Leroy <maxime@leroys.fr>
Signed-off-by: Vladimir Medvedkin <vladimir.medvedkin@intel.com>

fix_subject: mem: fix multi-process crash due to fbarray placement
fix_message:
mem: fix multi-process crash due to fbarray placement

Since the VA space of all memseg lists is reserved in one go, it is
reserved before the memseg lists are created. The fbarray of each list
is allocated from the same VA allocator, so the first fbarray now ends
up right after the end of the memseg lists.

On Linux, the PCI bus maps device BARs in the primary process starting
at the end of the memseg lists (pci_find_max_end_va()), using it as an
address hint. This address is now taken by the fbarray, so the hint is
not honored and the kernel places the first BAR elsewhere in the mmap
area, among the shared libraries and thread stacks.

With VFIO, secondary processes map BARs at the addresses chosen by the
primary process, using MAP_FIXED, which replaces any existing mapping.
As the mmap area layout is randomized for each process (ASLR), the BAR
can overlap the libraries or stacks of the secondary process, which are
then replaced. This intermittently crashes secondary processes during
EAL init, for example dpdk-proc-info. On arm64 with 64K pages, this
was seen in about one in ten secondary process starts.

Create the memseg lists before reserving the VA space, so that, as
before that change, nothing is mapped right after the memseg lists and
the BARs can be placed there again. The VA space is still reserved in
one go.

Also destroy the memseg lists created so far if a later step fails,
since their fbarrays now exist before the VA space is reserved.

Fixes: 3368bc8600e8 ("mem: allocate all VA space in one go")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Aarnav JP <ajp@marvell.com>
Acked-by: Anatoly Burakov <anatoly.burakov@intel.com>

fix_subject: net/af_packet: fix build with old kernel headers
fix_message:
net/af_packet: fix build with old kernel headers

The PACKET_IGNORE_OUTGOING socket option is used unconditionally,
but it was only added to the uapi headers in Linux 4.20. The build
fails on distributions shipping older kernel headers, like RHEL 8
(kernel-headers-4.18.0-193.el8, gcc 8.5.0):

  ../drivers/net/af_packet/rte_eth_af_packet.c:
    In function 'rte_pmd_init_internals':
  ../drivers/net/af_packet/rte_eth_af_packet.c:1057:41:
    error: 'PACKET_IGNORE_OUTGOING' undeclared
    (first use in this function); did you mean 'PACKET_OUTGOING'?
      rc = setsockopt(qsockfd, SOL_PACKET, PACKET_IGNORE_OUTGOING,
                                           ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
                                           PACKET_OUTGOING
  ../drivers/net/af_packet/rte_eth_af_packet.c:1057:41:
    note: each undeclared identifier is reported only once
    for each function it appears in

Define the constant when the headers lack it, as is already done for
PACKET_FANOUT_FLAG_IGNORE_OUTGOING.

Kernels older than 4.20 also reject the option with ENOPROTOOPT,
which makes the probe of a single-queue port fail when
ignore_outgoing is enabled. In this case, fall back to filtering
outgoing packets in the PMD, as already done for multi-queue ports
on kernels without PACKET_FANOUT_FLAG_IGNORE_OUTGOING support.

DPDK documents Linux 5.4 as the minimum kernel, but the PMD already
tolerates older kernels for multi-queue ports. Do the same here
instead of failing the probe, for example on the 4.18 kernel of
RHEL 8.

Fixes: 3db7aa7868b2 ("net/af_packet: use kernel to filter single-queue Rx")

IPsec flow parsing leaves the pattern-match item allocated after

when no metadata output is requested.

Free the pattern-match item after parsing and free the parsed flow item

fix_message:
net/iavf: fix memory leaks around IRQ resources

`iavf_config_rx_queues_irqs()` allocates a queue-vector map and may
enable eventfds and allocate an interrupt vector list. If queue startup
then fails, those resources remain allocated. The queue-vector map is
also retained after a normal stop, leaking it across start/stop cycles.

fix_subject: net/memif: fix some interrupt FD leaks
fix_message:
net/memif: fix some interrupt FD leaks

Fix several resource leaks in error handling and cleanup paths:

In memif_socket_create(), when rte_intr_callback_register() fails,
return via error path instead of returning directly, ensuring sockfd,
sock and intr_handle are properly cleaned up.

In memif_socket_init(), when rte_hash_add_key_data() fails, clean up
the newly created socket including unregistering callback, closing fd
and freeing intr_handle for listener sockets.

fix_subject: common/cnxk: use one interrupt handle per vector
fix_message:
common/cnxk: use one interrupt handle per vector

All MSI-X vectors were registered on pci_dev->intr_handle, rewriting
its fd before each rte_intr_callback_register(). Since EAL references
the caller's handle instead of a copy, all vectors share one interrupt
source whose fd is read live, so only the last vector is polled.
Mailbox replies are lost, probe times out, and the cleanup path leaves
a closed fd in the source, making the interrupt thread panic in
epoll_ctl().

Register each vector on its own handle, tracked in a list so that
unregister uses and frees the same handle. Reject duplicate vector
registration, close the vector's own eventfd on unregister, and unwind
all error paths of plt_irq_register().

Fixes: c663018eb7f3 ("interrupts: do not duplicate interrupt handles")

fix_subject: net/iavf: fix AdminQ polling after interrupt setup failure
fix_message:
net/iavf: fix AdminQ polling after interrupt setup failure

The device alarm skips AdminQ processing when the PF advertises WB_ON_ITR.
However, this capability does not guarantee that interrupt registration
succeeds. FreeBSD nic_uio cannot register device interrupts, so the VF
still needs alarm polling. Without it, commands such as RSS configuration
and statistics queries time out and device configuration fails.

Record whether AdminQ uses alarm polling instead of deriving that choice
from the PF capability. Initialize polling on each device initialization
and disable it only after interrupt registration and enablement succeed.
If enablement fails, unregister the callback before retaining polling.
Keep the shared PHC alarm and unconditional alarm cancellation unchanged.

Validated the backport to 25.11.4 on FreeBSD with an E810 ice PF: the stock
PMD failed configuration in three trials, while the correction passed 45
queue restarts, 42 full device resets and 6,432 exactly received frames.

Fixes: 388f0b348065 ("net/iavf: reuse device alarm for PHC sync")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

fix_subject: net/ice: fix inconsistent state on FDIR failure
fix_message:
net/ice: fix inconsistent state on FDIR failure

FDIR creation programs the hardware rule before inserting its software
hash entry. If insertion fails, creation returns without removing the
hardware rule or releasing its counter, and MARK parsing may remain
enabled despite no flow handle being returned.

Reserve the hash entry before programming the rule, and release the
counter if reservation fails. Remove the reserved entry if hardware
programming fails. Enable MARK parsing only after both steps succeed.

fix_message:

check, unlike the SSO sibling path. A CPT completion processed before the
callback is registered or after it is cleared caused a NULL

fix_subject: net/dpaa2: fix integer overflow in CCSR region mapping
fix_message:
net/dpaa2: fix integer overflow in CCSR region mapping

In lsx_ccsr_map_region(), PAGE_SIZE is defined as
sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE), which returns a signed long and may be
negative on error. The value was used directly in size_t
comparisons and mmap() length calculations, leading to an
integer overflow (Coverity CID 49765682).

The old code also computed the mapping length without taking
the address offset within the page into account. As a result,
regions crossing a page boundary might not be fully mapped.
The mapping size must cover the entire range from the
page-aligned start address through offset + len.

Fix by validating the page size returned by sysconf(),
deriving the page mask from the validated value, and using
RTE_ALIGN_CEIL(offset + len, page_size) to calculate the
mapping length.

Coverity issue: 49765682
Fixes: f023d059769f ("net/dpaa2: support recycle loopback port")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Hemant Agrawal <hemant.agrawal@nxp.com>

fix_subject: net/iavf: fix bandwidth config of unshaped queues
fix_message:
net/iavf: fix bandwidth config of unshaped queues

When configuring queue bandwidth via virtchnl in iavf_hierarchy_commit(),
an entry in the bandwidth configuration array is allocated for each queue
node. However, the driver only populated queue_id and tc for nodes that
had an active shaper profile.

Because the configuration buffer is zero-initialized with calloc(), any
unshaped queue node left its entry with queue_id 0, tc 0, and zero rate
limits. Consequently, the PF interpreted each unshaped queue entry as a
request to reset queue 0 to default bandwidth, leaving the actual target
queue untouched on the PF. Any previously configured rate limit on that
queue remained active, even across subsequent queue enables or process
restarts.

Fix this by setting queue_id and tc for every queue node, ensuring
unshaped queues properly send zeroed shaper rates for their own queue ID
so the PF restores their default bandwidth.

Fixes: 5779a8894d15 ("net/iavf: support queue rate limit configuration")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Dawid Wesierski <dawid.wesierski@intel.com>
Acked-by: Bruce Richardson <bruce.richardson@intel.com>

fix_subject: acl: reject rules with inverted range
fix_message:
acl: reject rules with inverted range

rte_acl_build() doesn't check that for a RANGE field the low bound
(value) doesn't exceed the high bound (mask_range). Field types are
known only from the rte_acl_config passed to rte_acl_build(), so
rte_acl_add_rules() doesn't validate ranges. Such a rule is accepted,
and then:
- for a 1-byte field the build crashes with a NULL pointer
  dereference in acl_gen_node();
- for a 2-byte field (e.g. port range 80..22) the build succeeds,
  but the rule matches every value of the field instead of none.

The check was done only for the legacy ipv4vlan rules
(acl_ipv4vlan_check_rule(), now in app/test). Validate RANGE fields
of all rules in acl_check_bld_param(), together with the rest of the
build parameters, and fail rte_acl_build() with -EINVAL.
Add a test case with the generic API.

Fixes: dc276b5780c2 ("acl: new library")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Acked-by: Konstantin Ananyev <konstantin.v.ananyev@yandex.ru>

fix_subject: net/mlx5: fix local and host representor name collision
fix_message:
net/mlx5: fix local and host representor name collision

On BlueField with a single uplink and host PF, representor port names
omit the controller index. A local representor (pf0vf0, controller 0)
and a host representor (c1pf0vf0, controller 1) with the same index
were both named <BDF>_representor_vf0. Whichever was probed first took
the name. Probing the other one returned EEXIST, which is treated as
already spawned, so the attach succeeded silently without a new port.

Add controller and PF indexes to the names of local representors on
BlueField, detected by the presence of a host PF, for example
<BDF>_representor_c0pf0vf0 and <BDF>_representor_c0pf0sf0.
The host PF representor can also report controller 0, so it is
excluded explicitly. Host representor names are unchanged.

Also log a notice when a requested representor is already spawned,
so that probing it again is no longer silent.

Fixes: cb95feefdd03 ("net/mlx5: support sub-function representor")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Acked-by: Dariusz Sosnowski <dsosnowski@nvidia.com>

interrupt FD was invalid, so the caller saw 65535 packets sent after
ring->head had already been published. The FD can legitimately be -1:
memif_init_queues() only warns and continues when eventfd() fails. Skip

real count.

dma/dpaa: fix data validation on completion path

fsl_qdma_data_validation() runs on every completion. It is a
byte-by-byte software compare of the transferred data, which belongs to
debugging and not to the datapath, where it costs a read-back and a
compare of every descriptor that completes.

Gate it behind s_data_validation, which is off by default, so the
compare is skipped unless it is explicitly asked for.

fix_subject: mempool/dpaa: fix use-after-free during pool cleanup
fix_message:
mempool/dpaa: fix use-after-free during pool cleanup

dpaa_mbuf_free_pool() freed the pool private data and then wrote to it:

	rte_free(mp->pool_data);
	bp_info->bp = NULL;

bp_info is DPAA_MEMPOOL_TO_POOL_INFO(mp), which is mp->pool_data, so
both refer to the same allocation. Clearing bp_info->bp after the
rte_free() writes into freed memory.

Clear the field before releasing the allocation, and free bp_info
directly rather than the alias.

fix_subject: net/failsafe: fix queue release without sub-device op
fix_message:
net/failsafe: fix queue release without sub-device op

Some PMDs do not implement that op, so the function pointer is NULL.
Calling it unconditionally could dereference a NULL pointer and crash

fix_subject: net/txgbe: fix DAC hotplug on AML40 with auto-negotiation
fix_message:
net/txgbe: fix DAC hotplug on AML40 with auto-negotiation

Hot-plugging a DAC cable while an Amber-Lite 40G port is running
does not bring the link up.

First, the AML40 never delivers the GPIO interrupt for module
insertion or removal, so txgbe_dev_detect_sfp() is not called and the
new module is never identified (the 25G part is not affected). Poll
the module-present level every 2 seconds instead. Identification is
attempted only when the cached module state is not present, and the
poll re-arms itself only while the SFP/AN73 alarm gate is set, so that
it cannot survive txgbe_dev_stop(). With an empty cage that poll
reported the absence and cancelled the AN73 watchdog on every pass;
do both only when the cached state changes to not present.

Second, on AML40, an unsupported QSFP identifier, or a QSFP module
with no supported capability bit, previously left the cached state as
not present. The poll then repeated the delay and I2C reads
indefinitely, and the latter case also repeated module and link setup.
Record these modules as unknown and return not supported so polling
resumes only after an observed removal.

Third, when the port is started with no module plugged in,
txgbe_set_link_to_amlite() times out and leaves hw->link_valid false.
The xpcs path of txgbe_setup_phy_link_aml40() never restores it, so
txgbe_e56_check_phy_link() and txgbe_check_mac_link_aml40() keep
forcing the link down even once AN73 has brought it up. Restore
link_valid on the xpcs path, as the non-xpcs path already does.

Fixes: a2d92608d3b0 ("net/txgbe: add GPIO configuration")
Fixes: f7cfc21e9f75 ("net/txgbe: fix link stability for 40G NIC")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Zaiyu Wang <zaiyuwang@trustnetic.com>

fix_subject: net/iavf: fix interrupt callback race on close
fix_message:
net/iavf: fix interrupt callback race on close

In iavf_dev_close(), rte_intr_callback_unregister() can return -EAGAIN
while the interrupt thread is executing a callback for the same source.
The return value is ignored, leaving the callback registered.

Close hits that window. It sends virtchnl commands (RSS, promiscuous
mode, flows), and iavf_dev_interrupt_handler() handles each response.
The handler clears the pending command before it returns, so the
thread waiting in iavf_wait_for_msg() can go on to the unregister
while the interrupt thread is still inside the callback. This is
likely when the two threads share a CPU.

Two failures follow:
- The interrupt thread resumes the callback after
  rte_eth_dev_release_port() has set dev->data to NULL, and
  iavf_handle_virtchnl_msg() dereferences it: segmentation fault.
- The callback returns, but its source stays registered after the
  port is closed. At rte_eal_cleanup(),
  pci_vfio_unmap_resource_primary() closes the interrupt eventfd, and
  the next rebuild of the epoll set aborts the process:
    EAL: PANIC in eal_intr_thread_main():
    Error adding fd 49 epoll_ctl, Bad file descriptor

Use rte_intr_callback_unregister_sync(), as ice_dev_close() does. The
iavf_dev_init() error path has the same pattern; fix it too.

The sync variant waits for a running callback to return. It would
spin forever only if called from iavf_dev_interrupt_handler() itself,
and that handler never closes or re-initializes the port: it hands PF
events and resets to the iavf-event thread with iavf_dev_event_post().
A close from any other interrupt thread callback, such as an alarm,
returns at once, because the iavf source is not active then.

Fixes: 22b123a36d07 ("net/avf: initialize PMD")
Fixes: e35a5737a746 ("net/iavf: unregister interrupt handler before FD close")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Marek Kasiewicz <marek.kasiewicz@intel.com>

fix_subject: net/iavf: fix interrupt callback race on close
fix_message:
net/iavf: fix interrupt callback race on close

In iavf_dev_close(), rte_intr_callback_unregister() can return -EAGAIN
while the interrupt thread is executing a callback for the same source.
The return value is ignored, leaving the callback registered.

Close hits that window. It sends virtchnl commands (RSS, promiscuous
mode, flows), and iavf_dev_interrupt_handler() handles each response.
The handler clears the pending command before it returns, so the
thread waiting in iavf_wait_for_msg() can go on to the unregister
while the interrupt thread is still inside the callback. This is
likely when the two threads share a CPU.

Two failures follow:
- The interrupt thread resumes the callback after
  rte_eth_dev_release_port() has set dev->data to NULL, and
  iavf_handle_virtchnl_msg() dereferences it: segmentation fault.
- The callback returns, but its source stays registered after the
  port is closed. At rte_eal_cleanup(),
  pci_vfio_unmap_resource_primary() closes the interrupt eventfd, and
  the next rebuild of the epoll set aborts the process:
    EAL: PANIC in eal_intr_thread_main():
    Error adding fd 49 epoll_ctl, Bad file descriptor

Use rte_intr_callback_unregister_sync(), as ice_dev_close() does. The
iavf_dev_init() error path has the same pattern; fix it too.

The sync variant waits for a running callback to return. It would
spin forever only if called from iavf_dev_interrupt_handler() itself,
and that handler never closes or re-initializes the port: it hands PF
events and resets to the iavf-event thread with iavf_dev_event_post().
A close from any other interrupt thread callback, such as an alarm,
returns at once, because the iavf source is not active then.

Fixes: 22b123a36d07 ("net/avf: initialize PMD")
Fixes: e35a5737a746 ("net/iavf: unregister interrupt handler before FD close")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Marek Kasiewicz <marek.kasiewicz@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Dawid Wesierski <dawid.wesierski@intel.com>
Acked-by: Bruce Richardson <bruce.richardson@intel.com>

fix_subject: fib6: fix tbl8 reservation with RCU defer queue
fix_message:
fib6: fix tbl8 reservation with RCU defer queue

Currently, `trie_modify()` admits an update when `rsvd_tbl8s`, the number
of tbl8 levels the route set needs, fits the pool. The dataplane update
then takes tbl8s only within this reservation and is not expected to
fail half way.

In `RTE_FIB6_QSBR_MODE_DQ` mode, a tbl8 released by an update goes to the
defer queue and returns to the pool only once readers report a quiescent
state. Meanwhile `rsvd_tbl8s` already dropped if a prefix was deleted.
The deferred tbl8s are out of the pool but not accounted for, so while a
reader holds the grace period an add may run out of tbl8s inside
`modify_dp()`.

Fix it by counting the tbl8s used by the dataplane in `cur_tbl8s`, which
was unused so far. The tbl8s taken from the pool but not used,
`tbl8_pool_pos - cur_tbl8s`, are those waiting in the defer queue. Take
the reservation of an added prefix before writing the dataplane, and
check at the start of `modify_dp()` that the reserved tbl8s plus the
deferred ones fit the pool. If they do not, reclaim the defer queue once,
and return `-ENOSPC` before touching the dataplane if they still do not
fit.

Bugzilla ID: 1970
Fixes: 200ccb9ebd8e ("fib6: implement RCU rule reclamation")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Reported-by: Maxime Leroy <maxime@leroys.fr>
Signed-off-by: Vladimir Medvedkin <vladimir.medvedkin@intel.com>

fix_subject: ethdev: prevent overflow in indirect flow action conversion
fix_message:
ethdev: prevent overflow in indirect flow action conversion

The second pass of rte_flow_conv_actions() copies indirect action
handles whenever the destination size is nonzero, even if the buffer
does not cover the corresponding action entry. This writes beyond
the caller's buffer when an indirect action follows the last entry
that fits. The same applies to deprecated SHARED actions now that
their handles are preserved in the same branch.

Require the destination size to cover the full action entry before
writing its handle.

Fixes: fb131e295ea8 ("ethdev: fix indirect action conversion")

fix_subject: ethdev: fix MACsec item support in flow conversion
fix_message:
ethdev: fix MACsec item support in flow conversion

RTE_FLOW_ITEM_TYPE_MACSEC was never added to rte_flow_desc_item[].
The table uses designated initializers, so the MACSEC slot is zero
filled: its name is NULL and its size is zero.

As a result, RTE_FLOW_CONV_OP_ITEM_NAME on MACSEC passes a NULL
source to strlcpy(), and rte_flow_copy() as well as the pattern
conversion operations reject any pattern containing a MACSEC item
as an unknown item type.

Add the missing descriptor entry.

fix_subject: net/iavf: centralize memory management for flows
fix_message:
net/iavf: centralize memory management for flows

Flow engines currently distribute rule allocation and cleanup between the
parser, engine create and destroy callbacks, and generic flow code. This
leads to a lot of potential for memory leaks and bugs. In particular, one
of the issues currently present is that when PF initiates reset, we are
meant to just drop all flows without sending any virtchnl commands, but
because not all engines implement the `free` callback, some flows will be
leaked.

To address that specific leak as well as all other potential leaks due to
misuse of memory by engines, use parser-allocated rule objects as the
persistent rules and centralize their lifetime in the generic flow layer.
This requires fixing all engines to not manage their own memory:

- Allocate the final FDIR rule in the parser, use it for action checks,
  and remove the per-VF scratch configuration.
- Have FSUB create adopt its parser-produced rule instead of allocating
  and copying a second object.
- Build the final RSS configuration in the parser and remove the
  intermediate RSS metadata, including its unused raw-pattern flag.
- Let generic flow code free rules on validate, create failure,
  successful destroy, and uninit; remove engine-specific free callbacks
  and rule frees from destroy callbacks.

Fixes: 4dad1a6815d6 ("net/iavf: skip flow flush during PF-initiated reset")
Fixes: ff2d0c345c3b ("net/iavf: support generic flow API")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Anurag Mandal <anurag.mandal@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Anatoly Burakov <anatoly.burakov@intel.com>
Acked-by: Bruce Richardson <bruce.richardson@intel.com>

fix_subject: net/ice: fix read clock to use PHC hardware time
fix_message:
net/ice: fix read clock to use PHC hardware time

The ice_read_clock() function was incorrectly using clock_gettime()
with CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW to return system time instead of the actual
hardware PHC time. This caused txtime scheduling to use a completely
different time base than the PHC, resulting in all scheduled timestamps
being interpreted as past time by the hardware.

Replace the system clock read with ice_timesync_read_time() which reads
the actual PHC register value, ensuring the application can compute
correct future timestamps relative to the hardware clock.

Fixes: 327fe144ca39 ("net/ice: support clock read")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

Signed-off-by: Soumyadeep Hore <soumyadeep.hore@intel.com>
Acked-by: Bruce Richardson <bruce.richardson@intel.com>

fix_subject: net/gve: introduce Tx packet preparation for DQO format
fix_message:
net/gve: introduce Tx packet preparation for DQO format

Before this patch, packets that are invalid in the DQO format with
respect to offloads, descriptor limits, or packet size limits, are
dropped by the driver without any form of recourse for the application,
potentially leading to a disruption in traffic that can be hard to
debug.

Introduce tx_pkt_prepare for the DQ queue format to avoid dropping
packets without first giving the application a way to know that they
are invalid. For TSO packets, this method also computes the TCP
pseudo-header for packets with checksum offloading enabled. Note that
in this case, such packets must have L2/L3/L4 headers in the same mbuf
segment to pass tx_pkt_prepare.

Fixes: 403c671a46b6 ("net/gve: support TSO in DQO RDA")
Cc: stable@dpdk.org

fix_subject: bpf: fix ICMP sample checksum accumulation
fix_message:
bpf: fix ICMP sample checksum accumulation

The checksum helper advances by 256 bytes between body128 invocations,
but each invocation only sums 64 16-bit words (128 bytes). This leaves
parts of the quoted packet out of the ICMP checksum.

Rename the existing macro to body64 and compose body128 from two body64
invocations so that each invocation covers all 256 bytes.

Remove the hard-coded ICMPv6 checksums from the no-backend reply fixtures
and let Scapy calculate them independently. The existing
tc_nodeport_lb_no_backend and tc_lxc_lb_no_backend BPF tests exercise the
ICMPv6 error-reply paths and compare the complete response packets. They
fail with the original helper and pass with this fix, so a new end-to-end
scenario is not required for this checksum regression.

Fixes: #48297

cilium-cli: fix sysdump leaving CiliumCIDRGroups out of the bundle

Since cilium-cli v0.18.4 (June 2025) sysdump fails to collect the
CiliumCIDRGroups. The bundle of a cluster that uses CIDR groups
carries an empty ciliumcidrgroups-<ts>.yaml, as if the cluster had

fix_subject: maps/netdev: always create cilium_devices with BPF_F_NO_PREALLOC
fix_message:
maps/netdev: always create cilium_devices with BPF_F_NO_PREALLOC

The datapath declares cilium_devices with BPF_F_NO_PREALLOC
(bpf/lib/network_device.h), but the agent creates it with flags 0, to
which bpf.NewMap adds the preallocation flags of the map type. With
--preallocate-bpf-maps=true, a hash map gets no flag: the two
definitions differ. The datapath side got the flag in the commit below;
before it, the two differed with the default --preallocate-bpf-maps=false.

The agent and the loader then replace each other's pinned map: at
startup, the agent unpins the incompatible map and pins its own; the
next program loads find that map incompatible, each create a new, empty
map and race to pin it. The programs use maps the agent never fills, so
device_mac() and device_is_l3() see no device, and the losers of the
race fail:

  committing bpf pins: pinning map to /sys/fs/bpf/tc/globals/cilium_devices: file exists

Pass BPF_F_NO_PREALLOC explicitly, as the other maps the datapath
declares without preallocation do.

Fixes: #49881
Fixes: f5650d889753 ("bpf: let device_mac return zero MAC in case of missing device")
Signed-off-by: Lola Delannoy <lola.2lannoy@gmail.com>

fix_subject: loadbalancer: deduplicate socket termination per batch
fix_message:
loadbalancer: deduplicate socket termination per batch

Backend flattening introduced separate rows per service, address and
source priority. Deleting or marking unhealthy multiple rows for the same
address in one batch can therefore trigger repeated socket sweeps across
all eligible network namespaces.

Track the backend addresses examined within each batch before checking
for live references. The changes and liveness queries use the same
StateDB snapshot, so the liveness result only needs to be checked once
per address. Reset the tracked addresses for each batch so later changes
can request termination again.

Fixes: c0b0586457b1 ("loadbalancer: Flatten Backend")

Signed-off-by: Yusuke Suzuki <yusuke.suzuki@isovalent.com>

fix_subject: loadbalancer: preserve sockets to shared live backends
fix_message:
loadbalancer: preserve sockets to shared live backends

Fix a regression introduced by flattening the Backend representation.

Before flattening, services A and B sharing backend X were represented by
one row. Removing X from A updated that row:

    Backend{Address: X, Instances: {A, B}}
      -> Backend{Address: X, Instances: {B}}

With B's instance still alive, change.Deleted was false and IsAlive() was
true, so no socket termination was requested.

After flattening, rows are keyed by service, address and source priority:

    Backend{ServiceName: A, Address: X}
    Backend{ServiceName: B, Address: X}

Removing X from A deletes A's row, leaving:

    Backend{ServiceName: B, Address: X}

The unchanged condition sees change.Deleted=true and triggers socket
termination for X without checking B's row, potentially aborting B's
connections.

Before terminating sockets, check all instances at that address in the
same StateDB snapshot as the change iterator. Skip termination while any
instance is alive, including references from other services or sources,
restoring the behavior before flattening.

Fixes: c0b0586457b1 ("loadbalancer: Flatten Backend")

Signed-off-by: Yusuke Suzuki <yusuke.suzuki@isovalent.com>

fix_subject: iptables: add hairpin SNAT rule for BPF masquerade with kube-proxy
fix_message:
iptables: add hairpin SNAT rule for BPF masquerade with kube-proxy

With KPR=false, only ClusterIP services are in the BPF service map, so
a pod connecting to a LoadBalancer VIP, or to a NodePort on its own
node, goes through kube-proxy:

- Request, pod A -> VIP: bpf_lxc finds no service and passes it to the
  stack. kube-proxy DNATs it to backend pod B, and it leaves via
  cilium_host, over the tunnel if B is remote. The source stays A.
- Reply, B -> A: BPF delivers it straight to A, from bpf_overlay on A's
  node or from bpf_lxc if B is on the same node. It never passes the
  stack, so the DNAT isn't reversed and A resets the connection.

The "hairpin traffic that originated from a local pod" rule SNATs such
requests to the cilium_host IP, so the reply goes back through the
stack. It was only installed with iptables masquerading. Install it with
BPF masquerade too when KPR is off. In native routing, and for directly
routed nodes in hybrid routing, only same-node backends are affected:
requests to other nodes don't leave via cilium_host, so the rule doesn't
apply to them and the backend still sees the client's identity.

Fixes: 31eecce1835b ("agent: Remove deprecated EnableNodePort")
Fixes: 0823a7162e7f ("pkg/loadbalancer: limit service map entries when kpr=false")
Fixes: #48178
Signed-off-by: Maxim Skokov <skokovmaksimevg@gmail.com>

fix_subject: policy/compute: Ensure superseded policies are not leaked
fix_message:
policy/compute: Ensure superseded policies are not leaked

When a new policy computation replaces an existing policy entry in the
table, superseding the old one, the table kept storing the old one
unnecessarily. The SelectorPolicy object for each identity was kept
until an identity has a new policy computed for it again. Especially
with large L7 rules this adds up (because L7 rules can be complex).

This commit fixes this leak by not storing the old policy in the table
anymore. Instead, the compute cell only keeps it until it has superseded
it.

Memory growth in BenchmarkUpdatePolicyThroughput, before and after this
commit:

```
                             before     after
eps=100,  ids=100            5.41 MB    2.22 MB
eps=1000, ids=100           14.14 MB   11.07 MB
eps=100,  ids=20, http=40   15.93 MB    1.13 MB
```

Fixes: ee243265837 ("policy/compute: Add policy computation cell")
Signed-off-by: Chris Tarazi <chris@isovalent.com>

fix_subject: l2announcer: Ignore leader events of replaced services
fix_message:
l2announcer: Ignore leader events of replaced services

client-go does not wait for OnStartedLeading, so its event can arrive
after gcOrphanedService removed the service. If the announcer selected
the same Service again in the meantime, processLeaderEvent applies the
stale event to the old selectedService and removes the entries of the
new one, whose IP stays unannounced until another event recalculates
them.

This commit fixes it by dropping leader events whose selectedService
differs from the one in selectedServices.

This commit was prepared with AIL:3. I personally checked that a local
test replaying a late leader event fails without this change.

fix_subject: l2announcer: Fix deadlock between stop() and leader events
fix_message:
l2announcer: Fix deadlock between stop() and leader events

stop() runs on the main loop and waits for the service's leader
election to exit, but the election sends an event on its way out, on a
16-slot channel that only the main loop reads. Once the channel fills
up, for example when deleting 17 selected services at once, the main
loop hangs and the agent announces no new IP until it restarts. This
made GatewayHTTPListenerIsolation fail in 6 of the last 103 Gateway API
conformance push runs on main, with the agent stuck in:

  goroutine 677 [chan receive, 4 minutes]:
  github.com/cilium/cilium/pkg/l2announcer.(*selectedService).stop(...)

This commit fixes it by having stop() close a channel that the election
selects on next to the send, as stop() already resets the leader state.
On agent shutdown, the elections stop before the main loop, so their
events still arrive and withdraw the entries.

This commit was prepared with AIL:3. I personally checked that a local
test deleting 17 leading services blocks without this change.

fix_subject: bpf: edt: apply drop horizon to packets with a future timestamp
fix_message:
bpf: edt: apply drop horizon to packets with a future timestamp

When a packet arrives with a skb->tstamp later than the aggregate's next
departure slot, edt_sched_departure() stores that timestamp in t_last
as is. The drop horizon is only checked on the other branch, so a single
packet stamped beyond t_horizon_drop moves t_last that far ahead. Every
following packet of the endpoint then lands past the horizon and is
dropped with DROP_EDT_HORIZON until the clock catches up, regardless of
the rate the endpoint actually sends at.

Such timestamps are set by the sender, for example through SO_TXTIME,
and likely by TCP pacing once a long RTT sample has collapsed the
socket's pacing rate. FQ would drop the packet at its own horizon
anyway.

This commit fixes it by checking the horizon before updating t_last, as
the comment on the other branch already intends.

The conformance-kubespray entry has the paths-regex

which replaced the workflow's pull_request paths filter when it moved

fix_subject: gha/conformance-aws-cni: Fix CIDR lookup on pooled clusters
fix_message:
gha/conformance-aws-cni: Fix CIDR lookup on pooled clusters

The "Determine the native routing CIDR" step looks the subnet up by
steps.vars.outputs.cluster_name, the synthetic run name. A cluster
claimed from the pool carries its real eksctl name, so the lookup
returns nothing and the workflow installs Cilium with an empty

  Successfully claimed kubeconfig: cilium-pool-1-36-all-addons-1792966269-cf6b1a13-1792967328.yaml
  ...
  Native routing CIDR:

The 1.36 leg, the only one PRs run, claims from the pool whenever the
pool holds a cluster, so its agent configuration changes between runs.
The workflow disables masquerading, so the value does not change
traffic today. 730a69b7f9b6 (".github: fix EKS native-routing CIDR
lookup on pooled clusters") fixed the same lookup in conformance-eks.

This commit uses setup-cluster.outputs.cluster_name and fails the step
unless it finds exactly one CIDR, as conformance-eks does. The fresh
and pooled lookups we checked all return exactly one CIDR, so the check
only fires on a missed lookup.

This commit was prepared with AIL:3. I personally checked the CIDR
lookup logs of the pooled 1.36 legs in AWS-CNI run 40252738449 and EKS
run 40253811944.

fix_subject: pkg/ipam: preserve multi-pool allocators ordering when performing release
fix_message:
pkg/ipam: preserve multi-pool allocators ordering when performing release

In the multi-pool IPAM's `releaseExcessCIDRsMultiPool` method, a loop goes through the `ipAllocators` in reverse ordering to free up the newest CIDRs first. This loop then reconstructs the slice of `ipAllocators` in a reverse ordering and is copied to the pool's `ipAllocators` property. This means that each time this method is called, it flips the order of the CIDRs and pod IPs get spread out on different CIDRs instead of getting bin-packed on the oldest CIDRs.

This fixes this bug by reversing the `retainedAllocators` slice before copying it to the pool's `ipAllocators` thus maintaining the original ordering. This also adds a unit test to make sure ordering is always preserved.

Fixes: 3b7deba08d88dbab534c87680075e9fa9537df41

Signed-off-by: Alex Melhem <alex.melhem@datadoghq.com>

fix_subject: policy/compute: Merge retries of failed computations
fix_message:
policy/compute: Merge retries of failed computations

A failed policy computation is requeued by appending a new request for
its identity. If a request for the same identity came in while the
batch was computed, both are queued. The next batch then computes the
identity twice, and the second result is dropped when its
CompareAndSwap fails.

Requeue failed computations with enqueueLocked instead, which merges
the retry with a pending request for the same identity.

Fixes: ee243265837 ("policy/compute: Add policy computation cell")

fix_subject: policy/compute: Drop results for identities removed mid-computation
fix_message:
policy/compute: Drop results for identities removed mid-computation

Previously, if an identity is removed while computing policy for it, or
just before it's queued, the result was still committed to the
policy-computations table. Nothing deletes that row afterwards. It keeps
the SelectorPolicy and its SelectorCache references alive. Which is
basically a leak.

This commit tracks the local identities in the policy computer.
Computations for identities that no longer exist are not queued, and
results for identities removed since their request was queued are
dropped and their policies detached instead of being committed.

fix_subject: fqdn: Order endpoint regeneration after DNS proxy initialization
fix_message:
fqdn: Order endpoint regeneration after DNS proxy initialization

Endpoint regeneration can allocate DNS redirect ports before the DNS
proxy registers its listener port, leaving redirects pointing at a
different port.

Provide a DNS proxy initialization promise and await it in the endpoint
restorer before publishing restored endpoints or completing initialization.
The shared restoration barriers then order host endpoint initialization
and endpoint API operations, including when restoration is disabled.
The wait runs in a background job so Hive startup remains unblocked.

If binding a restored port fails, log a warning and retry with an
OS-assigned port. An explicitly configured port remains mandatory.

fix_subject: mapsweeper: Stop removing the always-created SRv6 maps
fix_message:
mapsweeper: Stop removing the always-created SRv6 maps

Since commit f9a26eae31bf ("maps/srv6map: always create and pin
srv6maps"), the agent creates and pins the five cilium_srv6_* maps at
startup even with SRv6 disabled, so that program loads never race to
create them. RemoveDisabledMaps still lists them as maps of a disabled
feature, so the sweep after endpoint restore unpins all five. bpf_lxc
still references cilium_srv6_policy_v4 from nodeport_rev_dnat_ipv4,
and the first bpf_lxc loads after the sweep each create and pin it.
When two of them overlap, the second pin fails the endpoint
regeneration:

  loading eBPF collection into the kernel: map cilium_srv6_policy_v4: pin map to /sys/fs/bpf/tc/globals/cilium_srv6_policy_v4: file exists

This commit drops the SRv6 maps from RemoveDisabledMaps. The five empty
maps then stay pinned with SRv6 disabled, which costs nothing since the
agent recreates them at every start. Entries from an earlier
SRv6-enabled run stay inert, since the policy lookups need a VRF ID and
every VRF lookup sits behind the runtime SRv6 config.

This commit was prepared with AIL:3. I personally checked that the new
subtest fails on unmodified main.

Fixes: #49483
