fix_subject: endpoint: Avoid double wait for the initial endpoint policy
fix_message:
endpoint: Avoid double wait for the initial endpoint policy

For background, ComputeInitialPolicy computes an endpoint's policy at
the start of its first regeneration, before the regeneration takes a
build permit. The permit comes from the endpoint build queue, which
limits how many endpoints are built at once, so a regeneration can wait
there behind other builds. Computing the policy first means Envoy gets
the initial policy early, while the endpoint waits.
runPreCompilationSteps is meant to reuse that result unless policy
changed in the meantime. runPreCompilationSteps depends on
policyResult.endpointPolicy being set, but setDesiredPolicy clears that
field once it has installed the policy as the desired one, so
runPreCompilationSteps never reuses policyResult.

The above then results in every first endpoint regeneration waiting
for the policy computation result again, adding the redirects again
and distilling the policy a second time. This includes every endpoint
restored when the Agent starts.

This has happened since c597c56b6c3, which removed the revision check
that made regeneratePolicy skip the second computation. The
endpointPolicy check itself dates back to 351dce163cb.

This commit fixes this by dropping the endpointPolicy check, and making
the reuse check compare both the identity and the identity revision of
the result. The identity revision is bumped when the labels change,
before the new identity is set. The identity check ensures that the
identity did not change between the policy computation and the
regeneration that reuses it.

In theory, this halves the policy calculation of an endpoint's first
regeneration, since it now does that work once instead of twice.

Fixes: c597c56b6c3 ("endpoint: Plumb policy computer")
Signed-off-by: Chris Tarazi <chris@isovalent.com>

fix_subject: loadbalancer: Fix leak of expanded NodePort frontends with two scopes
fix_message:
loadbalancer: Fix leak of expanded NodePort frontends with two scopes

The BPF reconciler expands each NodePort frontend (0.0.0.0) into one frontend per NodePort node address. It records the expanded addresses in `nodePortAddrByPort`, keyed by address family, L4 proto and port. The key does not include the scope.

A NodePort service whose `externalTrafficPolicy` and `internalTrafficPolicy` differ will have two frontends for the same port, one in the external scope and one in the internal scope. Both frontends use the same `nodePortAddrByPort` entry. After a user deletes the service, `Delete()` for the first frontend removes the expanded frontends of its scope and then deletes the shared entry. `Delete()` for the second frontend then finds no addresses and does not remove the expanded frontends of its scope.

The leaked frontends keep their service map slots, their reverse NAT entry, their service ID, and their backend references. The reconciler still holds these references, so pruning does not remove the entries. Only an agent restart clears them. The same collision leaks the external scope frontends when a service changes from two scopes to one and a user deletes it later.

Add the scope to `nodePortAddrKey`, so that each scope tracks its own expanded addresses. Also add a script test for the delete case and for the change from two scopes to one.

Fixes: a552f78ac58f ("experimental/lb: Add NodePort and HostPort addr refresher")

Signed-off-by: Salvatore LaMendola <salvatore@lamendo.la>

fix_subject: gha/setup-aks-cluster: Allow the runner's Actions range
fix_message:
gha/setup-aks-cluster: Allow the runner's Actions range

AKS restricts the cluster's API server to the runner's egress IP as a
/32. On a KPR AKS + WireGuard leg, the runner also egressed from
48.214.55.35 while the cluster allowed 48.214.55.37/32, the same second
SNAT address that stalled GKE before 40fb3d2db6ce
("gha/setup-gke-cluster: Allow the runner's Actions range"). 56 of 2,816
API handshakes waited for SYN 10 or 11, 37 never completed, and execs
timed out [1]:

  ⚠️  Retrying exec after attempt 1/3: command failed (pod=kube-system/cilium-nxf4q, container=cilium-agent): exec attempt timed out after 10s: context deadline exceeded

This commit moves the GKE lookup of the runner's GitHub Actions range
into its own action and makes setup-aks-cluster use it too, so AKS
allows the runner's range, here 48.214.0.0/17, next to the /32. The
trade-off is the one GKE took: other Azure customers and GitHub-hosted
jobs share that block, so they can reach the API server's
unauthenticated endpoints, and a leaked credential works from them.

This commit was prepared with AIL:3. I personally checked the probe
summary in the job log of run 39742934082.

Fixes: b7f1f7ae1e71 ("fix: azure aks apiserver hardening")

fix_subject: daemon: Warn instead of error for BPF masquerade on upgrades
fix_message:
daemon: Warn instead of error for BPF masquerade on upgrades

Maxim reported that Cilium can now fail to start on upgrades when we
switch to BPF masquerading, if using --egress-masquerade-interfaces or
--enable-masquerade-to-route-source. These options are not supported by
BPF masquerading and currently cause an error.

This commit switches the errors to warnings. For
egress-masquerade-interfaces, the correct fix is to use --devices. We
warn the user so that they can add their interfaces to --devices is
that's not already the case. For enable-masquerade-to-route-source,
there is no BPF equivalent, so we fallback to iptables masquerading and
notify the user via the warning.

In both cases, the warning can be avoided: the
egress-masquerade-interfaces case can be avoided by setting --devices
and unsetting --egress-masquerade-interfaces; the
enable-masquerade-to-route-source can be avoided by disable BPF
masquerading explicitly.

Fixes: c94bb1e13546 ("daemon, helm: Enable BPF masquerading by default")
Reported-by: Maxim Skokov <skokovmaksimevg@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Paul Chaignon <paul.chaignon@gmail.com>

fix_subject: daemon: Don't warn when disabling BPF masquerading
fix_message:
daemon: Don't warn when disabling BPF masquerading

We currently warn when disabling BPF masquerading because IPv4 and IPv6
masquerading are disabled. That makes the AWS-CNI workflow fail. I think
we should just emit an info message in this case: if the user explicitly
disabled masquerading, then there's no point warning about the

fix_subject: ipam: prevent full resyncs from restoring deleted instances
fix_message:
ipam: prevent full resyncs from restoring deleted instances

NodeManager.Delete calls DeleteInstance to forget the instance of a
deleted CiliumNode, so that a node rejoining with a changed
configuration triggers InstanceSync in Upsert. DeleteInstance takes only
m.mutex. If it runs after a full resync read the cloud API, the
resync replaces the cache with a snapshot that still holds the instance.
A rejoining node then finds HasInstance true, skips InstanceSync, and
Node.recalculate() uses the stale snapshot until the next full resync.

Take a read lock on resyncLock in DeleteInstance before taking m.mutex
in the AWS, Alibaba Cloud and Azure providers. NodeManager.Delete calls
DeleteInstance after releasing its own mutex, so waiting for an
in-flight full resync does not block Upsert and Resync.

Add a regression test per provider that pauses a full resync after its
cloud read and checks that an instance deleted in that window stays
deleted, and one that blocks DeleteInstance and checks that
NodeManager.Delete no longer holds its mutex.

This commit was prepared with AIL:3. I personally checked the three new
tests failing without the lock.

Fixes: c112a3e59dcc ("eni: fix new node not triggering creation of ENI")
Signed-off-by: André Martins <andre@cilium.io>

fix_subject: datapath: Fix NAT46x64 gateway prefix conversion panic
fix_message:
datapath: Fix NAT46x64 gateway prefix conversion panic

PR #43799 started populating the `nat_46x64_prefix` node config with
`IPv6NAT46x64CIDRBase.As4()`. The base is the IPv6 address `64:ff9b::`,
and `netip.Addr.As4()` panics on IPv6 addresses that are not IPv4-mapped,
so the agent crashes with "As4 called on IPv6 address" while building
the node configuration as soon as `--enable-nat46x64-gateway` is set.

The datapath only consumes the leading 32 bits of the RFC6052 prefix
(see `nat46x64_prefix_copy_v6()`), which is what the previous
`AsSlice()` based code passed. Take the first four bytes of `As16()`
instead, and add a regression test.

Fixes: b156a3abae ("bpf, nat46x64: move RFC6052 prefix into node config")

Signed-off-by: Hadrien Patte <hadrien.patte@datadoghq.com>

fix_subject: Fixed #37377 -- Fixed JSONField __in crash/wrong result for Value() primitives.
fix_message:
Fixed #37377 -- Fixed JSONField __in crash/wrong result for Value() primitives.

Refs #36689. 9b8e4c6d7d wrapped every Value() rhs param of a JSONIn lookup
in JSON_EXTRACT()/JSON_VALUE() assuming it was already JSON-serialized.
That only holds for Value(..., JSONField()); a bare Value("primitive") gets
an inferred non-JSON output_field (e.g. CharField), so its compiled param
was a raw primitive, not JSON text.

JSONIn.resolve_expression_parameter() now JSON-encodes the Value's raw
.value itself whenever its output_field isn't JSONField.

As a side effect, this also fixes Value(True)/Value(False) in __in, which
were previously compared as raw Python bools against the JSON-extracted
lhs and never matched.

Thanks Jacob Walls for the report.

The deprecation warning for double-dot variable lookups checked
str(filter_expression.var), which for constants is the resolved literal
value rather than a variable lookup. Templates containing string or translated
string literals with two consecutive dots, such as {{ "a..b" }} or

Variable lookup.

fix_subject: Fixed #37259 -- Restored support for old-signature Model.from_db() overrides.
fix_message:
Fixed #37259 -- Restored support for old-signature Model.from_db() overrides.

The fetch modes feature made all query iteration paths (ModelIterable,
RawModelIterable, and RelatedPopulator) call Model.from_db() with a
fetch_mode keyword argument. This crashed with a TypeError for models
overriding from_db() with the previously documented signature
from_db(cls, db, field_names, values).

Query iteration now detects, once per query rather than per row, whether
the model's from_db() accepts the fetch_mode keyword argument (or
**kwargs) and calls old-style overrides without it, emitting a
RemovedInDjango70Warning asking authors to add the argument.

Regression in e097e8a12f21a4e92594830f1ad1942b31916d0f.

fix_subject: Fixed #37262 -- Restored rendering of html-safe strings in form media.
fix_message:
Fixed #37262 -- Restored rendering of html-safe strings in form media.

`Media.__init__()` normalized every string js/css entry into `Script` or
`Stylesheet` objects. `SafeString` is a `str` subclass, so html-safe strings
such as `mark_safe("<script defer src=...></script>")`, a previously-documented
idiom for including complete asset tags, were treated as asset paths,
run through `static()`, and percent-encoded instead of being rendered
verbatim.

Leave objects providing `__html__()` un-normalized so that they take the
verbatim rendering path, restoring the Django 6.0 behavior.

Regression in 8096b5251090bf7539c59956e398b027c7525529.

co-authored-by: Johannes Maron <johannes@maron.family>

fix_subject: Fixed #37260 -- Made alterations between Python on_delete options noops.
fix_message:
Fixed #37260 -- Made alterations between Python on_delete options noops.

Support for database-level delete options removed "on_delete" from
`Field.non_db_attrs` because changes to or from the new `DB_CASCADE`,
`DB_SET_DEFAULT`, and `DB_SET_NULL` options require schema changes. As a
consequence, an `AlterField` changing only a Python-level `on_delete` option
(such as `CASCADE` to `PROTECT`) performs unnecessary schema changes when it
was previously a no-op at the database level.

This commit makes `ForeignObject.non_db_attrs` a property that includes
`"on_delete"`only when the option is not a database-level one, so that:

- Python-level to Python-level changes skip DDL again,
- changes to, from, or between database-level options still alter the
  field.

Regression in 0c487aa3a7b2417481bf48c1e5355c855873e210.

fix_subject: Fixed #37263 -- Fixed changelist __exact search crashes and over-matching.
fix_message:
Fixed #37263 -- Fixed changelist __exact search crashes and over-matching.

Search terms for non-text `__exact` `search_fields` entries were validated
with the model field's `formfield().to_python()`, which failed to reject
invalid terms for two kinds of fields:

- Fields with choices use `TypedChoiceField`, whose `to_python()` returns
  the raw string unvalidated, so any non-matching search term (e.g.
  `"john"` against an `IntegerField` with `choices`) reached the ORM and
  crashed the changelist with a `ValueError` (HTTP 500).

- `BooleanField` uses `forms.BooleanField`, whose `to_python()` maps almost
  any string to `True`, so an arbitrary search term OR-matched every row
  with a `True` value instead of matching nothing.

Boolean search terms are now parsed such that arbitrary strings do not
match anything, and Typed(Multiple)ChoiceField search terms now coerce
to the correct types.

Regression in 4cecf3039586ea738afafb9a28c946bff42c37c1.

Thanks Adam Johnson for the report and Sarah Boyce for the review.

Co-authored-by: Jacob Walls <jacobtylerwalls@gmail.com>

fix_subject: Fixed #37222 -- Fixed QuerySet.distinct() crash on duplicated selections.
fix_message:
Fixed #37222 -- Fixed QuerySet.distinct() crash on duplicated selections.

When two lookup paths resolve to the same column, values() selects that
column once per path, at a different position each time. get_distinct()
refers to such selections by expression, and PostgreSQL binds an
expression reference to the first position the expression is selected
at. Ordering referred to each selection by its own position, so the
later ones yielded sort keys that DISTINCT ON could not be matched
against:

    SELECT DISTINCT ON expressions must match initial ORDER BY
    expressions

Ordering now refers to the first position an expression is selected at
when distinct fields are used. Annotations take part in that, as
PostgreSQL binds to their position as well when they select an
expression first, but their alias keeps referring to their own position
since get_distinct() refers to annotations by alias. Raw selections are
left out as equal SQL is not necessarily interchangeable, e.g. two
volatile extra() selections must keep ordering by their own position.

Regression in 65ad4ade74dc9208b9d686a451cd6045df0c9c3a.

Thanks Robert Leach for the report and Simon Charette for the review.

fix_subject: vcpu: Complete pending I/O before honoring immediate_exit
fix_message:
vcpu: Complete pending I/O before honoring immediate_exit

Firecracker can acknowledge a pause after handling an MMIO or PIO exit
without completing the guest instruction. Commit 32cfc5e8db93
("skipped unnecessary kvm_immediate_exits") added a userspace
immediate_exit shortcut that skips KVM_RUN, but KVM requires re-entry
to finish I/O. Snapshots can then omit the pending RAM write or
register update because KVM does not expose the unfinished operation
in saved vCPU state.

Always issue KVM_RUN and let KVM complete pending I/O before returning
EINTR for immediate_exit, without executing further guest instructions.
Keep the existing EINTR flag clearing so the vCPU can resume normally.

The test runs a guest that loads a byte from an MMIO address into a
register, on both x86_64 and aarch64. After handling the MMIO exit, it
sets immediate_exit and calls KVM_RUN again. It checks that the register
holds the MMIO response, but the following guest instruction has not
executed. A final KVM_RUN checks that this instruction executes after
the flag has been cleared.

Fixes: 32cfc5e8db93 ("skipped unnecessary kvm_immediate_exits")
Signed-off-by: James Curtis <jxcurtis@amazon.co.uk>

fix_subject: fix(tests): retry start_screen_process on non-zero screen -ls
fix_message:
fix(tests): retry start_screen_process on non-zero screen -ls

start_screen_process() polls 'screen -ls' in a 30 x 1 s tenacity loop
to find the PID of the session it just started with 'screen -dmS'. The
loop only retries RuntimeError, which search_output_from_cmd() raises
when the command succeeds but its output does not match the session
name. Until screen has created the session socket, 'screen -ls' exits
1 with "No Sockets found in /run/screen/S-root." and check_output()
raises ChildProcessError instead, so the loop gives up on the first
attempt and spawn() fails with:

  E   ChildProcessError: screen -ls
  E   No Sockets found in /run/screen/S-root.
  E   Returned error code: 1

This failed test_firecracker_kill_by_pid (daemonize=False) in nightly
https://buildkite.com/firecracker/firecracker-pr-nightly/builds/4235
(-n 16 --dist worksteal). Firecracker was alive: its log shows "API
server started." and it answered the teardown API calls; 'screen -ls'
had run ~40 ms after 'screen -dmS' returned. The loop has never covered
this case: the original retry_call() predicate was also RuntimeError-
only while the command already ran with check=True.

Retry ChildProcessError as well, so a not-yet-listed session consumes
the 30 s budget instead of failing the test. A 'screen -ls' that keeps
failing still re-raises its last error after 30 attempts (reraise=True),
and the 'screen -dmS' call itself is still not retried.

Fixes: 48a51ad2d2fa ("tests: Run 'screen -ls' in a busy-waiting loop")
Signed-off-by: Riccardo Mancini <mancio@amazon.com>

fix_subject: test: restore vulnerability finding subset comparison
fix_message:
test: restore vulnerability finding subset comparison

The vulnerability file A/B test compares lists of dictionaries with <=.
Python treats this as lexicographical ordering, so the first result that
differs between revisions attempts to order dictionaries and raises a
TypeError. Identical A/B results previously hid the bug.

exceptions and vulnerable statuses as findings, and fail explicitly when

Use issubset() to allow B to remove findings while rejecting new

fix_subject: pci_mngr: Fix attach vs reset deadlock by releasing allocator lock early
fix_message:
pci_mngr: Fix attach vs reset deadlock by releasing allocator lock early

attach_pci_virtio_device() binds the resource allocator lock to a local
that lives until the end of the function, so it is still held across
attach_common(), which inserts the device's BAR mapping into the
mmio_bus. That is the resource allocator lock taken before the mmio_bus
lock.

Since the bus holds its read lock for the duration of a device access, a
device access can take the two locks in the opposite order: a guest MMIO
access that resets a virtio-pci device runs under the mmio_bus read lock
and calls reset_msix() -> KvmVm::create_msix_group(), which allocates
from the resource allocator. A device hotplug concurrent with a guest
resetting an existing device therefore deadlocks (ABBA).

Hold the resource allocator lock only for as long as allocating the BARs
needs it, so it is released before any bus is touched.

Fixes: 548d79224525 ("bus: hold the read lock during device accesses")
PR: https://github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/pull/6087
Signed-off-by: Ilias Stamatis <ilstam@amazon.com>

fix_subject: hypervisor: mshv: Fix cross-page accesses in the x86 emulator
fix_message:
hypervisor: mshv: Fix cross-page accesses in the x86 emulator

`HV_HYP_PAGE_MASK` is -4096, so the length of the first part underflowed
for every emulated cross-page access. Debug builds panic on the
subtraction, release builds when slicing the buffer with the wrapped

fix_subject: vmm: prefault: Release workers only after their thread startup
fix_message:
vmm: prefault: Release workers only after their thread startup

TL;DR: Fix performance regression, make large prefaults up to 4x faster

A recent addition [0] cleaned up and improved the prefaulting code, but
introduced a subtle severe performance regression. We forgot to wait
for each thread to actually finish its startup (libc, ruststd) routine.

Let each worker report from its own thread that it is ready, and
release the workers only once all of them did. The Barrier used before
aa74b1d13 did the same.

Microbenchmark: prefaulting the RAM of a 20 GiB VM (regions of 3 and
17 GiB, 1 + 4 workers) on a server (4x Xeon Gold 6154), and of a 12 GiB
VM (4 + 8 GiB, 1 + 2 workers) with 4 KiB pages on a laptop (AMD Ryzen 7
7840U) [units in s, median, less is better]:

                      server THP  server 4 KiB  laptop 4 KiB
  before aa74b1d13          1.61          2.98          0.89
  aa74b1d13                 3.75          6.97          0.86
  this commit               0.94          1.76          0.55

Fixes: aa74b1d13 ("vmm: Pin and parallelize memory prefault")
On-behalf-of: SAP philipp.schuster@sap.com
Signed-off-by: Philipp Schuster <philipp.schuster@cyberus-technology.de>

fix_subject: hypervisor: x86: Store all 8 bytes for MOV r/m64, imm32
fix_message:
hypervisor: x86: Store all 8 bytes for MOV r/m64, imm32

With a memory destination, `mov qword ptr [m], imm32` stored only the
low 4 bytes of the sign-extended immediate and left the upper 4 bytes
untouched. On MSHV, a guest using this instruction for an emulated MMIO
access therefore issued a 4-byte write instead of an 8-byte one. The
register form was not affected.

This regressed in 0c3ef986f ("hypervisor: emulator: rewrite MOV
emulation with get/set_op"), which replaced the u32tou64 operand size
with u32.

fix_subject: Prerender route handlers that await immediates (#101593)
fix_message:
Prerender route handlers that await immediates (#101593)

Route handlers still use the immediate-based prerender scheduling
introduced in PR #70208. Pages moved to timeouts in PR #84344, atomic
timer groups in PR #86093, and fast immediates in PR #86018. This left
route handlers that await immediates classified as dynamic even when
they perform no uncached I/O.

This change coordinates the final handler pass with atomic timers and
fast immediates. It tracks immediate work during cache warming and
preserves the native body-consumption window needed by in-memory Blob
responses. The regression tests cover handler and body scheduling, cache
warming, and asynchronous error propagation.

fix_subject: Add segment config parity regression tests (#100881)
fix_message:
Add segment config parity regression tests (#100881)

## Summary

Add webpack-compatible regression coverage to
`test/production/segment-config-precedence/segment-config-precedence.test.ts`
for six parity findings identified while reviewing #100210:

- Node-only custom 404 under an Edge root layout, in production and
development.
- Unequal sibling `dynamic`, `dynamicParams`, `revalidate`, and
`fetchCache` values, including exports on a slot layout.
- Runtime and region exports on `global-not-found`.
- An ordinary page alongside an explicit `@children/page`.
- `maxDuration` immediately above the u32 boundary, reusing the existing
boundary controls.
- Conflicting layout runtimes across the default ordered page
extensions.

Existing tests, their registrations and gates, original fixtures, and
`next.config.ts` are preserved. New page cases share the existing
webpack app/build. New known build-failing Turbopack cases use the
file's existing `@force-gate !turbopack` and build-path exclusion
patterns. The explicit `@children` fixture is injected into webpack's
app only: Turbopack's route-structure validation runs before build-path
filtering. The global-404 runtime mismatch uses the existing `@gate
!turbopack` pattern, which still exercises the assertion and detects
when the gate becomes stale.

Separate builds remain for the expected-invalid configuration tests and

fix_subject: Add a server-router regression gate: pnpm test-routing (#100812)
fix_message:
Add a server-router regression gate: pnpm test-routing (#100812)

## Summary

`pnpm test-routing` runs the e2e tests that check the server's routing
and HTTP behavior, first with `next start` and then with `next dev`,
through the existing `run-tests.js`. The suite passes on today's server,
so a failure after a change to the server is a regression. It's the gate
for consolidating the server and routing implementation.

- `test/routing-tests-manifest.json` is a v2 test manifest of whole
files: every test under `test/e2e/routing-server/`, plus 69 existing
suites that mostly test server routing. That's 87 files; start mode runs
86 and dev runs 80. Nothing is selected by test name, and a manifest
entry that matches no file fails the run.
- `scripts/test-routing.mjs` expands the manifest into explicit paths
for each mode and sets the same bundler environment as the CI jobs.
Turbopack is the default; `--bundler=webpack` and `--bundler=rspack`
also work, and the Rspack manifests narrow the list. It turns
`run-tests.js` retries off when a selected test directory has unstaged
changes, because a retry resets that directory with `git clean -fdx`.
- `test/e2e/routing-server/` adds 18 test files for payloads and body
limits, headers and cookies, streaming, compression, connection
lifecycle, route selection, routing phase order, Proxy, i18n, RSC
requests, caching, Draft Mode and image endpoints. Its README covers how
to run the suite.
- Tests assert what the server does today. Five check behavior today's
server doesn't have, so they run behind `@gate`, each with a TODO that
explains the failure and links the docs:
- In `next start`, hashed `_next/static` assets get the `Cache-Control`
from `headers()`, not the immutable policy that [the headers
docs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/headers#cache-control)
say can't be overridden.
- In `next start`, a `force-static` GET isn't cached when the same file
exports other methods, unlike what [the Route Handler caching
docs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers#caching)
describe.
- `next/image` advertises `images.path`, but the server only serves
`/_next/image` ([Image
docs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/components/image#path)).
- With a matching Proxy, Pages client navigation to a config redirect
keeps the source URL, unlike what `redirects.mdx` describes.
- webpack dev prints no conflict message for a page and a Route Handler
at the same URL. That's a bundler inconsistency, not a docs
contradiction: the build and Turbopack dev print one.
- Seven of the existing suites cover areas where `@next/routing` is thin
or where adapters already fail, so the gate also catches differences if
`next start` switches to `@next/routing`: dynamic-route matching
(`dynamic-routing`), the rewritten-path headers on RSC requests
(`rewrite-headers`), RSC query handling (`adapter-rsc-query-leak`),
WebSocket upgrades (`socket-io`), forwarded host and protocol
(`x-forwarded-headers`), and two suites left out of deploy runs
(`i18n-hybrid`, `app-custom-route-base-path`).
- Three more new tests are gated only on Vercel deployments, where CI
runs new tests: the adapter build answers `/_error` with 200, Proxy
without a matcher doesn't run for `/_next/image`, and
`skipProxyUrlNormalize` doesn't show Proxy the data URL as sent.
- `test/e2e/api-support` now reads large responses to the end and writes
the chunked response with backpressure. On Node.js 24, the 4 MB
response-limit case failed with `SocketError: other side closed` without
this.

This replaces the earlier version of this PR. That version added a
separate scheduler with test-name selection (`--suite-list` in
`run-tests.js`), contract IDs in test names, and expectations in
existing suites for behavior that isn't built yet: custom server
lifecycle, bundler selection, tsconfig reloading and dev route repair.
All of that is dropped. Its small fixes to existing tests (next-head,
OpenTelemetry, metadata-dynamic-routes) can come as separate PRs.

## Verification

- `pnpm test-routing` (Turbopack) on Node.js 24.22.2, after merging
canary: start passed 86 files in 11.3 min and dev passed 80 files in
10.7 min. In dev, `dynamic-routing` › "should resolve dynamic route href
for page added later" passed on retry; it passed 3 of 3 runs on its own.
- `pnpm test-routing --bundler=webpack`: start passed in 14.1 min and
dev in 15.4 min. In dev, `cancel-request/stream-cancel` passed on retry.
- After the test names were reworded: `pnpm test-routing
test/e2e/routing-server --retries 0` passed with both bundlers in both
modes.
- Not run locally: deploy mode, Rspack, the Cache Components jobs and
Node.js 20.9.0.
- Run the suite locally on Node.js 24.21 or later. Earlier versions lack
the [realpath fix](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/65113), and
without it a dev fixture can load React twice and time out.

fix_subject: Fix blocking revalidation for `fetch` and `unstable_cache` (#101077)
fix_message:
Fix blocking revalidation for `fetch` and `unstable_cache` (#101077)

With Cache Components enabled, a page that uses cached `fetch` calls or
`unstable_cache` can return a 500 during on-demand revalidation,
including blocking regeneration after `expire`. Both wrappers skip the
incremental cache lookup, so the final prerender cannot reuse the data
computed by the prospective pass. It repeats asynchronous work and fails
with `NEXT_STATIC_GEN_BAILOUT`.

The incremental cache now reads the Resume Data Cache (RDC) during
on-demand revalidation before it bypasses persisted entries. Both
`unstable_cache` and cached `fetch` calls use this path, so the final
prerender can reuse the prospective pass's result.

This extends the fix proposed in PR #100895 to cached fetches and
preserves the forced-refresh behavior introduced in PR #48516. The
incremental cache continues to apply its tag invalidation checks before
it returns an entry.

Fixes #99866
Closes #100895

fix_subject: Distinguish dynamic rendering from required prerendering (#101511)
fix_message:
Distinguish dynamic rendering from required prerendering (#101511)

The prerender classification introduced in #96080 uses `blocking` for
both required prerendering and request-time rendering with no initial
response. Those cases need different cache-miss policies.

This change adds `compute: 'dynamic'` for empty PPR outputs that permit
request-time rendering without a separate prerender first. The
`blocking` value now requires generation or revalidation before serving
a response when no usable cached prerender exists. The generated result
can still need request-time rendering. This requirement also applies
after an on-demand prerender expires or is evicted.

Outputs for paths not generated at build time use `empty/static` when
`ensureStatic = 'navigation'` guarantees static server output. Their
response is empty because no fallback is available, but generation must
produce static server output or fail validation. Concrete built paths
retain the classification of their own output.

This prepares #101309's full-route RSC classification and #101357's
request handling for the proposed update to nextjs/adapter-vercel#114.
That proposal maps `static` and `blocking` to `onMiss: 'sync'`, and
`dynamic` and `resuming` to `onMiss: 'dynamic'`. Static outputs avoid an
additional dynamic invocation, while other eligible misses can stream a
response alongside background prerendering.

The adapter draft still derives `onMiss` from `response`. It and the
shared metadata consumers need updating for this contract. Matching HTML
cache-miss handling in `next start` remains a follow-up for deployment
parity.

fix_subject: Reload on missed Turbopack startup CSS updates (#99963)
fix_message:
Reload on missed Turbopack startup CSS updates (#99963)

### What?

Recover missed Turbopack startup CSS edits with a full page reload,
while keeping ordinary CSS HMR state-preserving. Related: #99893; reuses
the version-mismatch recovery introduced in #97966.

### Why?

CSS can finish loading before the browser starts HMR. An edit in that
window leaves old CSS in the page, but initializing the browser from the
current WebSocket version hides the mismatch. The initial HTML needs to
carry the version it actually rendered, and the server must observe CSS
before any browser subscribes.

### How?

- Capture the client HMR version before rendering and emit
`__nextHmrInitialVersion` in an inline script **only in dev-server HTML
with Turbopack HMR**, using safe serialization, the existing CSP nonce
and Pages crossOrigin precedence.
- Use the HTML version as the first-connection fallback. Previously
observed WebSocket versions retain priority on reconnect. A stale
subscription reuses the existing reload message/handler.
- Await CSS-inclusive observation before serving HTML: App route client
output, Pages route client output, and Pages' global `_app` client
output. Pages chunks exclude dependencies already provided by `_app`, so
the global observer is necessary for a truly fresh Pages-first load.
- Reuse existing subscription ownership/deduplication and per-cycle
client-version accounting. Successful observation sends no
refresh/build-success message and does not invalidate the
server-component cache. Subscriptions remain disabled for one-shot
compilation. A genuinely missed startup JS output change can use the
same recovery path.
- Remove the previous startup stylesheet reconciliation/readiness
machinery and restore the original CSS loader. Remove Pages' duplicate
reload action; its existing guarded hot-middleware listener already
handles the message before and after hydration.

### Verification

Final local runs use isolated packages:

- **Turbopack: 26 passed** — repeated App → Pages → App startup races,
independent fresh Pages-only startup recovery, controlled delayed Pages
greeting delivery, no-edit controls, global `_app`
JS/CSS-dependency/error/config recovery, and all app-document rendering
tests.
- **Cache Components: 14 passed** — both startup/lifecycle fixtures.
- **Pages/MCP regressions: 41 passed, 10 snapshots** — full/hot reload,
error pages, syntax/runtime recovery and compile_route.
- **Webpack: 30 passed, 10 snapshots**; **production/start: 12 passed**.
Twelve local dev-Turbopack HMR cases are appropriately gated in those
modes; both unconditional HTML-absence assertions still run.
- **14 units passed**, including await-before-HTML, dedicated global
key, absent/dev-disabled hooks, setup rejection and cleanup-key
semantics.
- Full bootstrap, root/Next/runtime types, ESLint, Prettier and
whitespace checks passed. No snapshots changed.

Pre-fix isolated tests reproduced the missing crossOrigin and fresh
Pages-first `HTML 0 / greeting 0` failures. Tests now await actual first
greeting/subscription evidence rather than treating hydration or
socket-open as message readiness. They still require a newer first
greeting, the original HTML subscription version, exactly one recovery
navigation, current CSS, ordinary CSS state preservation and a real
reconnect. Each race browser closes before file restoration so it cannot
mask later startup detection.

Coverage limits: controlled delayed delivery is proven for Pages, not
App. Live custom/default `_app` endpoint-identity add/remove and native
subscription counts were not instrumented; code/dependency changes,
config replacement and cleanup-key semantics are covered. Switching
between distinct global CSS imports already produces competing reloads
with or without the new observer; that pre-existing behavior is a
separate follow-up, not ordinary same-file CSS HMR. Local browser runs
used Chromium. Native/runtime source is unchanged in this follow-up;
four earlier local **dev-profile** Rust snapshots are historical
evidence, not a new release-with-assertions run. No agent CI reruns were
performed, and local verification does not claim remote CI success.

fix_subject: Turbopack: add unit test coverage for FileSystemPath::hash_file (#97743)
fix_message:
Turbopack: add unit test coverage for FileSystemPath::hash_file (#97743)

### What?

Adds unit test coverage for `FileSystemPath::hash_file`, the helper
introduced in #97507. It pins the
contract per filesystem entry type: a regular file is hashed by its
content, a symlink by its *own*
link content (target and whether it is absolute or relative), and a
directory or a path that doesn't
exist can't be hashed at all.

Tests only — no production code is touched.

### Why?

`hash_file` exists because hashing a traced path through `read()` was
wrong: `read()` follows a
symlink, so a link pointing at a directory made the build fail outright
with
`reading file "…" Is a directory (os error 21)`, and a link pointing at
a file silently produced the
hash of the target's bytes. The latter matters because consumers of the
trace re-create a symlink
entry *as a symlink* (`copyTracedFiles` does `readlink` + `symlink`)
rather than copying the resolved
file, so the link — not the file behind it — is what actually gets
written out and therefore what the
hash has to describe.

Nothing guarded that. The distinction is invisible at the call site
(`hash_file` reads like an
ordinary "hash this path" helper) and "just read the file and hash it"
is a natural-looking
simplification, which is exactly how the original crash was introduced.
A missing symlink case is
also the kind of thing that only shows up in the wild, on someone else's
repository layout, at build
time.

### How?

The test drives a real `DiskFileSystem` over a temporary directory
rather than exercising
`LinkContent::hash` directly, because the bug being guarded lives in the
entry-type dispatch — which
branch gets chosen — not in the hashing itself. A test that hashed a
`LinkContent` it constructed
would still pass against the buggy implementation. It reuses the harness
style of the existing
`read_glob` tests (a `turbo_tasks::function(operation, root)` wrapper
read strongly consistently),
and creates symlinks through a helper that mirrors their platform
handling, using a junction point
for a directory link on Windows.

The interesting design point is how "the link is hashed, not its target"
is asserted. Doing it by
mutating a file and re-hashing would pull in filesystem watching and
invalidation, so it is expressed
structurally instead: two directories each contain a file of the same
name but with different
content, and each has a symlink pointing at it through the same relative
target. Those two links must
hash *equally* (proving the target's content is irrelevant) while a
third link with a different
target must hash *differently* (proving the target itself is what
counts). Both of those assertions
fail against the pre-#97507 behaviour, as does the symlink-to-directory
case.

The remaining cases cover a dangling link and a link whose target leaves
the filesystem root — both
still hashable, since they are still links — and assert that every
distinct link hashes distinctly,
so nothing collapses into one shared "is a symlink" hash. The two
assertions covering directories and
missing paths document today's hard-error behaviour and carry a comment
pointing at the open question
already noted in `hash_file` about whether those should return `None`
instead, so it is clear which
assertions to revisit if that changes.

### Verification

- `cargo test -p turbo-tasks-fs` (125 tests)
- `cargo clippy -p turbo-tasks-fs --all-targets`, `cargo check -p
turbo-tasks-fs --all-targets`
- Confirmed the test actually guards the regression: reverting the
symlink arm of `hash_file` to
`read().hash()` makes it fail with the original `Is a directory (os
error 21)` error, and it passes
  again once restored.

fix_message:
Serve cached misses from the filesystem route cache (#96230)

`getItem` stores `null` for paths that don't resolve, but checks the
cached value with `if (lruResult)`, so a cached `null` is never served:
every request for an unknown path — including every dynamic-route
request — re-runs the lookup. It's been this way since the cache was
introduced in #52492.

Return the cached entry whenever the key is present. This can't go
stale: in production the item sets are only populated during
`setupFsCheck`, and the LRU is disabled in dev.

Cached misses are stored as a dedicated sentinel instead of `null`.
Since serving a cached miss has no observable effect, no test can catch
this regressing — that is also why it went unnoticed. With the sentinel
it's a type error instead: reintroducing the truthy check fails `pnpm
types` (verified). Same pattern as `invalidSourceMap` in
`source-maps.ts`.

Stacked on #96229, which bounds what negative entries can retain.

## Test Plan

No direct test: the change is unobservable by design, and the existing
e2e suites assert that it stays that way. The regression guard is the
type system, as above. `test/e2e/app-dir/not-found/basic` passes in prod
mode (14/14), exercising the negative-cache path.

fix_subject: fix(sandbox): release one-shot timeout ids after they run (#96161)
fix_message:
fix(sandbox): release one-shot timeout ids after they run (#96161)

### What?

Fire-and-forget `setTimeout` calls in the Edge runtime sandbox (e.g.
from middleware) are tracked forever by Next.js's sandbox
`TimeoutsManager`, even after the timeout has run. In a long-lived
standalone/self-hosted server this makes tracked timeout resources grow
monotonically, producing step-like heap growth and eventual OOM.

### Why?

`TimeoutsManager.add()` pushes each timeout id into a `resources` array.
When a one-shot timeout fires naturally, `webSetTimeoutPolyfill`'s
`finally` clears the underlying Node timer (the workaround for
nodejs/node#53335) but never removes the id from the manager. The id is
dropped only if user code calls `clearTimeout(id)` or the whole module
context is torn down (`clearModuleContext`, introduced in #57235). The
natural-completion path — module context stays alive, timeout finishes
on its own — was missing, so ids accumulate for the lifetime of the
process.

### How?

- `TimeoutsManager.create()` now wraps the callback so the timeout
untracks its own id once it has run. The Node-timer workaround and the
`this`/args binding in `webSetTimeoutPolyfill` are preserved.
- Refactored the base `ResourceManager.remove()` into `untrack()` (stop
tracking) + `destroy()`, so natural completion can release tracking
without a redundant `clearTimeout`.
- Intervals are intentionally unchanged: they fire repeatedly and must
remain tracked until `clearInterval`/`removeAll`.
- Added a unit test covering natural release, no monotonic growth across
repeated rounds, the `clearTimeout`/`remove` path, callback `this`/args
binding, and that intervals stay tracked.

Verified: `pnpm --filter=next types` clean, prettier/eslint clean, and
the new unit test fails on the current behavior (reverting only the
release logic) and passes with the fix.

Fixes #95094

---

**Update:** this branch now lands @berry95's commit from #94794 first
(`Set`-based resource tracking, which also makes `untrack`/`remove`
O(1)), with the fix rebased on top.

fix_subject: fix(next/image): preserve image response after optimization (#96681)
fix_message:
fix(next/image): preserve image response after optimization (#96681)

Fork PR #96621 by @ceolinwill, re-opened as a branch PR so the "when
deployed" CI job can run — it requires Vercel deployment secrets that
GitHub does not expose to pull requests from forks, so it can never pass
on the original.

**The commit is unchanged and still authored by @ceolinwill.** Please
credit them; #96621 should be closed in favor of this one.

### What?

`getSharp()` calls `_sharp.block({ operation: ['VipsForeignLoad'] })` to
block every image loader, then unblocks a specific allowlist — and that
allowlist omitted `VipsForeignLoadSvg`. Because `_sharp` is a
module-level singleton, the block is process-wide and permanent: the
first `/_next/image` request in a process permanently disables Sharp's
SVG loader.

`ImageResponse` (`next/og`) rasterizes via resvg and then hands SVG to
Sharp, so once that loader is blocked it fails. The symptom is worse
than a bad image — the render throws `Input buffer contains unsupported
image format`, which surfaces as a **socket hang up / crashed response**
on any `ImageResponse` route requested after an uncached image
optimization in the same process.

Introduced by #96301, which aligned the Sharp allowlist with
`detectContentType()` but missed SVG.

Fixes #96612

### How?

Adds `'VipsForeignLoadSvg'` to the unblock list.

This does not weaken SVG protections for user-supplied images.
`detectContentType()` already returns SVG, and untrusted SVG is gated
separately by `dangerouslyAllowSVG`, which throws a 400 in
`imageOptimizer()` before Sharp is ever invoked. Unblocking the loader
only restores Sharp's ability to process SVG that Next.js itself
generates.

### Tests

The existing `og-api` test is extended to reproduce the exact
same-process ordering: render `/og-node`, perform an uncached
`/_next/image` optimization (asserting `x-nextjs-cache: MISS`, with a
random URL so it can't be served from cache), then render `/og-node`
again.

Verified locally that this fails without the one-line fix (`socket hang
up`, caused by `Input buffer contains unsupported image format`) and
passes with it.

No regressions in the SVG security coverage —
`test/e2e/image-optimizer/dangerously-allow-svg.test.ts` passes 94/94
including all `maintain vector svg` / blur-svg cases, and
`test/e2e/image-optimizer/image-optimizer.test.ts` plus the `og-*`
suites are green.

fix_subject: fix(forms): flush debounced descendant values when a field is touched
fix_message:
fix(forms): flush debounced descendant values when a field is touched

`markAsTouched()` synchronized a pending debounced value only on the
field it was called on. Its descendants were marked as touched, but
their pending values stayed unsynced.

`submit()` marks the root as touched before running the action, so
submitting with Enter while a debounced child still had focus ran the
action with the child's old value. Clicking a submit button hid the bug,
because the click blurs the input first.

This is a regression from #67453. Before it, `submit()` called the
public `markAsTouched()` on each active field, which flushed it.

Flush each field's pending value right after marking it as touched.
Disabled, hidden and readonly fields still aren't marked as touched, but
unlike before #67453 they are flushed too, so their pending value reaches
the model before the action reads it. Below them only fields that already
exist are visited, since a field that was never created can't have a
pending value.

Tested with new specs in `//packages/forms/signals/test/node:test`. The
specs for descendants, `submit()`, an invalid flushed value, a duration
debounce and sibling fields fail without the fix; another checks that
touching a form doesn't create the fields of a hidden subtree.

Fixes #71149

fix_subject: fix(core): remove attribute when img/video attr.src is null or undefined
fix_message: fix(core): remove attribute when img/video attr.src is null or undefined The workaround introduced in #71095 converted `null` and `undefined` to `''` in `unwrapImgVideoSrcValue()`. While this coercion is needed for DOM property bindings (`[src]`) to prevent browsers from stringifying `undefined` to `"undefined"`, it inadvertently affected attribute bindings (`[attr.src]`). In the attribute binding path, coercing `null`/`undefined` to `''` causes `` to set `src=""` on the element rather than removing the attribute via `removeAttribute()`. In standard HTML, `` causes the browser to trigger an `(error)` event on the element, breaking patterns relying on omitting the `src` attribute until a URL is available. This commit updates `unwrapImgVideoSrcValue` to accept an `isAttribute` flag and only coerces `null`/`undefined` to `''` for property bindings. Attribute bindings continue to unwrap bypassed safe values while preserving `null`/`undefined` so that `setElementAttribute()` removes the attribute.

The startup path treats a zero rotation interval as disabled, but

fix_subject: wgengine/netstack: don't half-close the backend's read side after EOF
fix_message:
wgengine/netstack: don't half-close the backend's read side after EOF

After copying from the backend to the client until EOF, forwardTCP shut
down the backend socket's read side. That does nothing on the wire, and
once the backend's FIN has arrived, macOS rejects shutdown(SHUT_RD) with
ENOTCONN (Linux does too once the socket reaches TIME_WAIT), so every
forwarded connection logged "backend -> client close connection: ...
socket is not connected". Keep only the CloseWrite calls, which are what
propagate the half-close.

The regression was introduced by 04d24cdbd4 (#16462), merged 2025-07-07.

Tested on Linux and on macOS 27 (arm64): the wgengine/netstack tests
pass on both. The same ENOTCONN failure was reproduced on macOS via the
identical pattern in net/socks5 (#21522).

Updates #21522
Updates #16462

Signed-off-by: Brad Fitzpatrick <bradfitz@tailscale.com>
Change-Id: I3e9b1d7f4a2c8e6b0f5d9a3c7e1b4f8d2a6c0e5b

fix_subject: net/socks5: don't half-close the read side after EOF, tear down on error
fix_message:
net/socks5: don't half-close the read side after EOF, tear down on error

Shutting down a socket's read side after its peer's FIN has arrived does
nothing on the wire and fails with ENOTCONN on macOS (and on Linux once
the socket reaches TIME_WAIT), so every cleanly half-closed connection
was logged as a failure and TestTCPHalfClose failed on macOS. Only
half-close the destination after EOF.

When one direction fails, one of the two sockets is dead. If the failure
was writing to it, the other direction is reading from that dead socket
and finishes on its own once it has drained what arrived before the
failure, so leave it alone rather than truncate the data. If the failure
was reading from it, the other direction may be blocked reading the live
peer, so close both connections to unblock it; nothing deliverable is
lost in that case.

Telling the two apart means wrapping the destination, which disables the
kernel splice fast path when both ends are bare TCP connections (about a
third of relay throughput on Linux loopback). That is accepted here: the
common userspace-networking and proxymux configurations wrap the
connections anyway, so they never had the fast path.

The regression was introduced by 027e249fcf (#21359), merged 2026-09-17.

Tested on Linux and on macOS 27 (arm64): the old test failed 49 of 50
runs on macOS; the new tests pass 200 iterations there and pass under
the race detector on Linux.

Fixes #21522
Updates #20883

Signed-off-by: Brad Fitzpatrick <bradfitz@tailscale.com>
Change-Id: I7c2e4a9d1b8f5e3c6a0d2f4b8e1c9a7d3f5b6e2c

fix_subject: configure DNS even when router.Set fails (#20488)
fix_message:
configure DNS even when router.Set fails (#20488)

* wgengine: configure DNS even when router.Set fails

Reconfig configured the router first and returned on any router.Set error,
before the DNS block ran. On a host where router config fails on every
reconfig -- e.g. a tun MTU below 1280 that breaks IPv6, or a kernel missing
netfilter features -- the OS resolver was never told about MagicDNS or the
tailnet search domain, so tailnet names failed to resolve with no DNS error
in the logs.

Record the router error and continue instead of returning on it, still
attempt dns.Set, and join the router, DNS, and VPN-reconfigure errors into
the return value. DNS stays after router config (still needed: some DNS
managers refuse to apply settings before the device has an address); only
the error coupling is broken. Fixes a regression from 84430cdfa (v1.8.0).

Updates #20447

Signed-off-by: Brendan Creane <bcreane@gmail.com>

* wgengine/router/osrouter: gate IPv6 on per-interface support, not just global

getV6Available reported IPv6 usable whenever the netfilter runner reported
global IPv6 support, missing the case where the kernel has IPv6 but has not
enabled it on tailscale0 specifically -- e.g. when the tun MTU is below the
1280-byte IPv6 minimum, so /proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/tailscale0 never exists
and the v6 address and route adds fail, aborting the whole Set. See #20447.

AND a per-interface check into getV6Available, evaluated per call so a later
Set picks up v6 if the interface gains it. All v6-gated operations funnel
through getV6Available, so Set now skips v6 gracefully instead of erroring.
Also remove the dead r.v6Available field that masked this with its global
name.

Updates #20447

Signed-off-by: Brendan Creane <bcreane@gmail.com>

On CPython 3.10.0, NodeId's cached-string attribute isn't initialized because of python/cpython#88815. Calling str() on it raises AttributeError and prevents pytest from starting.

fix_subject: Fix rootdir conftest fixtures not visible outside rootdir (#14683)
fix_message:
Fix rootdir conftest fixtures not visible outside rootdir (#14683)

A conftest located in the rootdir used to get an empty baseid (matching
every collected item), so its fixtures were visible session-wide. The
node-based scoping introduced in 46478fad5 (#14098, pytest 9.1) scoped it
to its own Directory node instead. When --rootdir points to a subdirectory
and tests/doctests are collected from a parent directory, that Directory is
not an ancestor of the collected items, so the conftest fixtures --
including doctest_namespace injections -- became invisible (NameError in
doctests).

Restore the pre-9.1 behavior by attaching the rootdir conftest to the
Session node, in both places a conftest is parsed: the initial-conftest
flush and the Directory collect report.

This is behavior-identical for normal layouts (the Session is an ancestor
of all items under the rootdir), preserves the #14004 sibling-leak fix,
and keeps fixture overrides working (a subdir conftest is still more
specific than the Session).

fix_subject: Flatten recursive extras introduced by scoped overrides (#23210)
fix_message:
Flatten recursive extras introduced by scoped overrides (#23210)

## Summary

A package-scoped override can add a dependency on the package’s own
extra even when its published metadata has no self-dependency. The
resolver checked only the declared dependencies before skipping
recursive extra expansion. This let an unexpanded extra reach PubGrub
and trigger a debug assertion during a fresh `uv lock`.

Include overrides scoped to the current package and version in that
check.

## Test Plan

The regression test pins `urllib3==2.2.1` and adds `urllib3[socks]`
through a scoped override. On the original resolver, the test reproduced
`extras not flattened for urllib3`. With the fix, locking succeeds and
`uv tree --frozen` shows `pysocks` as an ordinary dependency of
`urllib3`.

- `cargo test --locked -p uv --test lock
lock::lock_project_with_scoped_override_recursive_extra -- --exact`
- `cargo fmt --all --check`

fix_subject: Resolve export extra activation globally (#22751)
fix_message:
Resolve export extra activation globally (#22751)

## Summary

This PR fixes the `uv export` slowdown introduced in #22234 (and
reverted in #22750) while retaining correct activation of transitive
extras.

We replace repeated propagation of growing activation maps with symbolic
package and extra reachability. Extra activation is then resolved across
the whole graph, so sibling branches share the same activation facts. If
recursive extra conditions leave any emitted package's inclusion
unresolved, we return an error.

| Workload | Before #22234 | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Original 19 exports, wall time | 0.519 s (0.509–0.533) | 0.499 s
(0.460–0.502) |
| 1,000 packages, 500 transitive marker inputs, CPU time | 78.1 ms
(76.3–81.1) | 12.0 ms (11.8–12.3) |

## How it works

The exporter needs a marker for each package: the environments in which
that package should appear. We compute it in two stages:

1. **Propagate reachability symbolically.** Following a dependency edge
combines the parent's reachability marker with the edge's marker using
`and`; alternative paths are combined with `or`. Package and extra
reachability are distinct: an edge requesting `foo[ssl]` reaches both
`foo` and `foo[ssl]`, but reaching `foo` alone does not enable its `ssl`
dependencies. Conflict activations remain symbolic during this
traversal.
2. **Resolve activations globally.** We combine the markers for reaching
each extra into a global activation equation. For example, if the only
request for `foo[ssl]` is on Linux, its activation is the Linux marker
everywhere it is referenced, including on sibling branches.

Activation equations without cycles are evaluated in dependency order.
For a cycle, we compute lower and upper bounds: where an activation is
definite, and where it remains possible. Positive cycles cannot justify
themselves (`a = a` resolves to false); negative cycles can leave the
bounds apart. We substitute the resulting bounds into each package's
marker and report an error if the uncertainty could change an emitted
package's inclusion. This is conservative: we do not exhaustively search
for a consistent selection, so even a lock with a unique consistent
selection can be rejected.

Keeping activations symbolic lets us combine complete paths before
resolving them, preserving correlations between alternative branches. We
revisit changed work and substitute activation conditions directly into
marker expressions without expanding them into disjunctive normal form.

fix_subject: [ty] Avoid widening compatible generic return alternatives (#29578)
fix_message:
[ty] Avoid widening compatible generic return alternatives (#29578)

Since #28303, when a generic call inference has multiple valid
solutions, we will intersect the return types resulting from
specializing with each valid solution. This approach has various caveats
discussed in the description of that PR. One of them is that sometimes a
call with an invariant return type (e.g. `list[T]`) can be validly
inferred as returning e.g. either `list[int]` or `list[str]`, but not
both simultaneously (consider if it actually returns `[]` -- it can be
viewed as either kind of list, but not both at the same time).
Intersecting `list[int]` and `list[str]` would result in `Never`, which
is wrong: the call can return.

For this reason, we skip intersecting return types if they vary in an
invariant type.

But in some cases one specialized return type is a subtype of all the
other ones. In this case it's safe to go ahead and prefer the narrower
type, even if they vary in invariant position and thus we wouldn't
otherwise intersect them.

This avoids a regression in #29236.

fix_subject: [ty] Preserve all alternatives in bounded intersections (#27898)
fix_message:
[ty] Preserve all alternatives in bounded intersections (#27898)

Bounded intersection expansion could silently drop alternatives after
the first four members of a union. The first union is intentionally
exempt from the expansion budget, but ignoring a failed insertion did
not actually insert the omitted member. This let the helper return a
partial type as though it were exact, causing false-positive diagnostics
such as the regression exposed by #27664.

Apply the budget exemption inside candidate insertion. Preserve every
alternative of the first union, while continuing to return `None` if
later expansion exceeds the budget.

Fixes astral-sh/ty#4335.

## Test plan

- Unit tests cover late union members surviving an intersection in
either operand order, the single-union fast path, and genuine budget
exhaustion returning `None` instead of a partial result.
- Mdtests cover redundant upper bounds on five-member gradual unions,
including a reduced recursive-alias regression with `Divergent` members.

fix_subject: [ty] Report override conflicts introduced by new bases (#28530)
fix_message:
[ty] Report override conflicts introduced by new bases (#28530)

## Summary

We now report override conflicts introduced by an additional base, even
when the subclass method matches its first parent's signature:

```python
from typing import Any

class Base[T]:
    def method(self) -> T:
        raise NotImplementedError

class Strings(Base[Any]):
    def method(self) -> str:
        return ""

class Concrete(Base[int]): ...

class Child(Strings, Concrete):
    # Previously accepted; now invalid-method-override.
    def method(self) -> str:
        return ""
```

Previously, we suppressed this error as an existing violation on
`Strings`, even though `Strings` only inherits `Base[Any]` and its
override is valid. We now check the parent's own ancestor
specializations before suppressing a diagnostic. Existing parent
violations remain reported only once, including violations of methods
inherited implicitly from `object`.

Follow-up to #28172. This missing diagnostic also occurs on that PR's
base.

fix_subject: [ty] Diagnose invalid __getattr__ calls (#27502)
fix_message:
[ty] Diagnose invalid __getattr__ calls (#27502)

## Summary

Previously, an invalid `__getattr__` method caused us to report that the
requested attribute was missing, even though Python actually invokes the
method and raises `TypeError`:

```py
class Example:
    def __getattr__(self) -> str:
        return "fallback"

Example().missing  # error: [invalid-attribute-access]
```

We now propagate failed implicit `__getattr__` calls through the
generalized member-lookup error introduced in #27400, so the diagnostic
identifies the invalid call and preserves the method's return type for
error recovery.

This applies to instance and metaclass attribute lookup, including
incompatible attribute-name parameters. Literal-restricted `__getattr__`
methods continue to treat unsupported names as missing attributes, and
already-defined attributes still bypass the fallback.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/135.

fix_subject: [mypyc] Fix lambdas in generator expressions consumed by builtins (#22225)
fix_message:
[mypyc] Fix lambdas in generator expressions consumed by builtins (#22225)

A generator expression that contains a lambda needs a lightweight
comprehension scope so that the lambda can capture the loop variables.
The special cases for tuple(), set(), sum(), any(), all(), next() and
other builtins that consume a generator expression didn't set up the
scope, so calling such a lambda raised UnboundLocalError, e.g.
`tuple((lambda: x) for x in range(3))`.

Move the scope helper to for_helpers.comprehension_scope and use it in
all these special cases.

This fixes a regression from #21009.

Also fix a few other closely related issues that came up when testing
the fix.

Add significant test coverage since these features seem to have a
high density of issues.

fix_subject: fix: measure nested transitions before applying their starting styles (#18647)
fix_message:
fix: measure nested transitions before applying their starting styles (#18647)

Fixes #18421 (regression from #16035, which re-broke the #4784
scenario).

Since #16035 the dummy delay animation runs with `fill: 'forwards'`, so
an intro's `t = 0` styles (for `slide`, `height: 0`) apply the moment
the transition is created and stay applied until the real animation
starts a frame later. Transition functions of other elements in the same
batch run after that and measure a collapsed DOM. With nested intros
(the TreeView from the issue), intro effects run deepest-first, so every
ancestor's `slide` captures a height where its children are pinned at 0.
On the issue's REPL every `<ul>` animates `0px -> 36px` (the height of a
single row) and then jumps to its real size when the animation finishes,
which is the "children pop out" behavior from #4784.

The fix waits one microtask before applying the initial styles and
creating the dummy, the same way deferred transitions (`crossfade`)
already work in `animate()`. Everything in the batch measures the DOM
first; the microtask still runs before the next paint, so elements never
render unstyled and the #14732 behavior is preserved. Verified in a real
browser that a delayed intro (`delay: 300`) stays held at `height: 0`
for the whole delay, including the first painted frame.

Most of the diff is the existing dummy/onfinish block moving into
`queue_micro_task`; hiding whitespace shows the actual change.

fix_subject: feat(trim-paths): stabilize `profile.trim-paths` (#17488)
fix_message:
feat(trim-paths): stabilize `profile.trim-paths` (#17488)

*[View all
comments](https://triagebot.infra.rust-lang.org/gh-comments/rust-lang/cargo/pull/17488)*

# Stabilization report: `profile.trim-paths`

Resolves rust-lang/cargo#12137
Resolves rust-lang/rust#111540
RFC: <https://rust-lang.github.io/rfcs/3127-trim-paths.html>

## What is stabilized

The rustc side `--remap-path-scope` was already stabilized in Rust 1.95
via rust-lang/rust#147611

This stabilizes the Cargo side:

* `profile.<name>.trim-paths = "none" | "object" | "all"`
  in both manifest and config
* The remap rules of how Cargo passes `--remap-path-{prefix,scope}`.
  The exact remap prefixes still stay unspecified.
* The unremap file `<artifact>.trim-paths.json` (schema v1),
  which is emitted beside final artifacts when debuginfo is on.
* `CARGO_TRIM_PATHS_SCOPE` and `CARGO_TRIM_PATHS_REMAP` for build
scripts.

When this is merged and sync in rust-lang/rust,
we'll also stabilize

* The `rust-gdb` and `rust-lldb` unremap loaders.
`RUST_GDB_TRIM_PATHS=unstable` and `RUST_LLDB_TRIM_PATHS=unstable` are
not needed anymore.

See doc for details:

https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/blob/8814ead110e36ed8fdcf1fdd4009baf82bd78523/doc/book/src/reference/unstable.md?plain=1#L1441-L1645

## What is not stabilized / included

* This doesn't guarantee full sanitization. It is a best-effort feature.
* Other `--remap-path-scope` values in rustc (`macro`, `diagnostics`,
`debuginfo`, `coverage`),
  boolean values, and comma-separated list options.
  These are removed in rust-lang/cargo#17432.
  They can come back later when needed.
* A default trim-path value for built-in profiles.
  RFC originall proposed to set `release` to `"object"`.
  This is left for future when this is more adopted and battle-tested.
We have loose stability guarantee for changing profile settings anyway.
* `__CARGO_RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP_WS_REMAP`.
  This stays as an internal thing between rustc bootstrap and cargo
  (see rust-lang/cargo#17349, rust-lang/cargo#17366)
* Doctest remapping and `documentation` scope.
  This will be integrated in the future incrementally
  when those scopes and features are stable.
* The exact remap prefixes are unspecified as documented.
  However, in practice,
  rustc bootstrap and debugger depend on the stabilized shape,
  so any change needs careful coordination with them.
* Unremap files for artifact deps: deferred, non-blocking.
* `build-rs` API for the two build script variables: deferred,
non-blocking.
* If there are new kinds of artifacts, we can decide whether to remap
freely.

### Doors closed

* The trim-paths profile key name, its shape, and its options.
* The unremap file name suffix `.trim-paths.json` and the v1 schema.
* The environment variable `CARGO_TRIM_PATHS_SCOPE` and
`CARGO_TRIM_PATHS_REMAP`.

## Post-RFC changes

* rustc removed `split-debuginfo` scopes,
  and Cargo followed and stopped caring split debuginfo.
* The RFC remapped the current package to relative paths and every
dependency to `<name>-<version>`.
  In rust-lang/cargo#17302 we chose workspace members relative remap,
  so debuggers resolve workspace sources with zero configuration.
The RFC worried that relative paths only work when running from the
right directory,
and symbolication tools need a second process for joining workspace
relative paths.
THe unremap file has `workspace_root`, so the join is fairly mechanical.
  Remap prefixes are unspecified anyway,
  so we can still change if it turns out not ideal.
* The unremap file is new (introduced in rust-lang/cargo#17303),
  for helping debugging find sources,
  as well as our keeping remap rules unspecified.
  The RFC had no answer about this.
* `CARGO_TRIM_PATHS_REMAP` build script env is new.
It lets build scripts forward the same rules to C/C++ compilers to flags
like `-fmacro-prefix-map`.
  `cc-rs` has integrated that since rust-lang/cc-rs#1794.

## Feedback

* rustc bootstrap builds the compiler and standard library with
`trim-paths`
  via rust-lang/rust#161049 since 2026-09-02.
This exercises the sysroot remap and the workspace prefix override in
rust-lang/rust CI.
* `cc-rs` forwards the remap rules to C/C++ compiler since 1.3.0:
<https://github.com/rust-lang/cc-rs/releases/tag/cc-v1.3.0>
* Zulip thread: [#t-cargo > stabilization plan for
`-Ztrim-paths`](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/246057-t-cargo/topic/stabilization.20plan.20for.20.60-Ztrim-paths.60/with/622955580)
* Call for testing posted on 2026-09-09
*
https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/12137#issuecomment-5688438901
* Included in TWiR issue 669
<https://this-week-in-rust.org/blog/2026/09/16/this-week-in-rust-669/>

## Known limitations

This sanitization is best-effort. See

* rustc:
<https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/remap-source-paths.html#caveats-and-limitations>
* Cargo:
<https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/blob/8814ead110e36ed8fdcf1fdd4009baf82bd78523/doc/book/src/reference/unstable.md?plain=1#L1603-L1626>

## Implementation

### History

| PR | Merged | Title |

|--------|------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| #12625 | 2023-10-31 | implement RFC 3127 `-Ztrim-paths` |
| #12900 | 2023-10-31 | set env `CARGO_TRIM_PATHS` for build scripts |
| #12908 | 2023-11-02 | merge `trim-paths` from different profiles |
| #13118 | 2023-12-06 | assert `OSO` and `SO` cannot be trimmed |
| #14389 | 2024-08-12 | rustdoc supports trim-paths for diagnostics |
| #14908 | 2024-12-09 | use Path::push to construct remap-path-prefix |
| #14917 | 2024-12-11 | use stable hash from rustc-stable-hash |
| #15614 | 2025-06-02 | remap all paths to `build.build-dir` |
| #15621 | 2025-06-02 | enable more tests for windows-msvc |
| #16536 | 2026-01-21 | `--remap-path-scope` stabilized in 1.95-nightly
|
| #17104 | 2026-06-15 | emit `CARGO_TRIM_PATHS_REMAP` for build.rs |
| #17221 | 2026-07-15 | exercise GDB on windows-gnu |
| #17302 | 2026-08-03 | unambiguous and reversible remap rules |
| #17303 | 2026-08-04 | emit unremap files for final artifacts |
| #17326 | 2026-08-07 | exercise unremap files with debuggers |
| #17338 | 2026-08-08 | `/cargo/deps` fallback sources |
| #17337 | 2026-08-10 | workspace remap under -Zroot-dir |
| #17349 | 2026-08-11 | honor workspace prefix override from env |
| #17366 | 2026-08-26 | custom workspace-relative member paths remap |
| #17424 | 2026-09-02 | remove default scope from release profile |
| #17425 | 2026-09-02 | docs: add limitations and polish |
| #17432 | 2026-09-04 | limit options to `none\|object\|all` |
| #17476 | 2026-09-15 | unremap file in one JSON doc |
| #17491 | 2026-09-21 | `build-rs` support |

### Test coverage

* Remap for each dependency kind
* `"object"` with every `split-debuginfo` mode
* `"all"` diagnostics remapping for rustc and rustdoc
* The new build-script environment variables.
* Real world debugger exercises with GDB, LLDB, and CDB
* unremap files with rebuilds, `cargo clean`, JSON messages
* rustc bootstrap workspace prefix override
* `-Zbuild-std` backtraces show `/rustc/<hash>` paths

## Follow-ups after stabilization

* [ ] Revisit reproducibility issues, such as
  * rust-lang/cargo#13586
  * rust-lang/cargo#15122
  * rust-lang/cargo#7645
  * rust-lang/cargo#10915
Absolute paths of workspace and `CARGO_HOME` still get into
`-Cmetadata`/`-Cextra-filename`/fingerprints.
With `trim-paths = "object"` we might be able to also trim paths in
those places.
* [ ] Revisit a new default for built-in profiles e.g., `release`
* [ ] In rust-lang/rust stabilize loader logic in
`src/etc/gdb_trim_paths.py` and `src/etc/lldb_trim_paths.py`
* [x] A new issue for `build-rs` adding `CARGO_TRIM_PATHS_SCOPE` and
`CARGO_TRIM_PATHS_REMAP` support
* [ ] A new issue for supporting doctest remapping and documentation
scope.
* [ ] Track unremap files support in artifact dependencies tracking
issue

fix_subject: Number input regression (#26369)
fix_message:
Number input regression (#26369)

# Objective

Fix a regression caused by #26284 where the number input reverts to the
previous value on focus loss.

## Solution

Updated the observer that triggers when a new number value is inserted;
this now overwrites the value even if the digits are the same, so long
as we're not editing and text edits are queued.

Note that a dev-dependency on `bevy_clipboard` was necessary for the
tests. Since `bevy_text` already depends on this, there should be no
impact.

## Testing

Manual test and unit tests.

Verified that the unit tests catch the regression.

reviewed by the author.

fix_subject: `GhostNode` z-ordering fixes and regression tests (#26255)
fix_message:
`GhostNode` z-ordering fixes and regression tests (#26255)

# Objective

`ui_stack_system` no longer flattened `GhostNode`s during the tree walk,
so children of `GhostNode`s weren't sorted.

Follow up to #25653.

## Solution

- Split up the UI root nodes query into one for ghosts and one for
non-ghost roots.
- Reuse the local child buffer cache to store the list of UI stack roots
descended from ghosts.
- In `update_uistack_recursive`: don't push ghosts onto `UiStack`, then
collect a ghosts children as normal but early return. This results in
the collected children being hoisted up a level.

The take and collect hack to preserve the child cache's allocation feels
a bit nasty. But I took it from elsewhere in Bevy, so I guess it must be
sound.

## Testing

Includes six new regression tests.

## AI Disclosure

Had astra check the logic, it identified some labelling errors in the
regression tests, and wrote the
`nested_ghosts_preserve_stacking_contexts` test.

fix_subject: Fix viewport node sizing regression (#26465)
fix_message:
Fix viewport node sizing regression (#26465)

# Objective
Fix the bug that shows up in the scroll example.
Issue #26440 


Found From investigating this discord comment
`Seems like a bug, did some bisecting, `e3d48d6` (**Update to Taffy 13
(#25413)**) is the bad commit`

https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/691052431974465548/1568021917175123969


## Solution
Our internal implicit viewport node is sized differently after
https://github.com/DioxusLabs/taffy/pull/960 because it gets an
automatic `auto` column and `auto` row track, so the column can grow to
fit the content rather than staying at 100% of the viewport. This is
non-intuitive to me but how grid works in CSS.

Adding minmax(0.0, fr(1.0) grid tracks fixes this and doesn't break
anything else. Unfortunately it does require a lazylock to include
non-empty vecs.

cargo fmt blew up the changes inside the styles but its just these lines
```
        grid_template_rows: vec![minmax(length(0.0), fr(1.0))],
        grid_template_columns: vec![minmax(length(0.0), fr(1.0))],
```

## Testing

- I retested the example and several others manually.

## AI Disclosure

I used claude code to check the differences between taffy commits, check
other layouts for issues, and suggest a solution.

fix_subject: Wait for the bin unpacking and uniform allocation pipelines before drawing (#26246)
fix_message:
Wait for the bin unpacking and uniform allocation pipelines before drawing (#26246)

# Objective

- Fixes regression from #23662: for one or two frames right after
start-up, some meshes are drawn with other meshes' materials (bindless +
GPU-driven indirect drawing).
- Fixes #26245

## Solution

- `PreprocessPipelines::pipelines_are_loaded` holds back
GPU-preprocessed draws until their compute pipelines are compiled.
- #23662 added the `unpack_bins` and `allocate_uniforms` (local scan /
global scan / fan) pipelines, but not to that check.
- While they're still compiling, both systems skip their dispatches ->
preprocessing runs on stale work items and stale
`IndirectParametersMetadata` (old `base_output_index`, counts not reset)
-> instances written into other draws' `MeshUniform` ranges -> drawn
with those draws' bindless material bind groups.
- Change: add both to the `Culling` arm of `pipelines_are_loaded`, with
`is_loaded` helpers for `BinUnpackingPipeline` and
`UniformAllocationPipelines`.

## Testing

- Reproducer (single file, in #26245): many quads with their own
materials, textures inserted late, camera panning; checks the first 60
frames by screenshot.
- Fresh launches with bad frames:
  - 0.20.0: 7/200 and 9/200 -> with fix: 0/600
  - main `ddd047d56`: 9/200 -> with fix: 0/200
- Logging skipped dispatches on unfixed 0.20.0: all 7 bad frames in 200
launches fell on frames in which `allocate_uniforms` skipped.
- Tested on Linux, AMD Radeon 8060S (RADV, Vulkan) only. Not tested:
Metal, DX12, WebGPU, other vendors.

# Showcase

Run the code in the linked issue with/without this patch.

## AI Disclosure

- The AI did: the reproducer, the bisect, finding the root-cause, the
diagnostic logging, the code change, and the measurements.
- I reviewed the change.

fix_subject: fix(tab_navigation): skip hidden subtrees during focusable gathering (#24968)
fix_message:
fix(tab_navigation): skip hidden subtrees during focusable gathering (#24968)

## Summary

Fixes #24935. Fixes a regression introduced in #24769 where menus would
auto-close immediately on open.

`gather_focusable` was skipping hidden entities from the focusable list
but still traversing their children. In the `feathers_gallery` example,
`FeathersMenuPopup` is always present in the hierarchy and shown/hidden
via `Visibility`. When a menu was opened, the popup's children had not
yet had their `InheritedVisibility` propagated, so they were visited,
found unfocusable, and focus fell outside the menu — which the menu
interpreted as a close signal.

## Solution

Move the children traversal inside the `InheritedVisibility` check in
`gather_focusable`, so that a hidden entity stops traversal of its
entire subtree. This matches the expected behaviour: if a container is
hidden, none of its descendants should be reachable via tab navigation.

## Testing

- Verified the `feathers_gallery` example no longer auto-closes menus on
open.
- Existing tab navigation tests continue to pass.
